claim: EDIT 4(b) treats virus_covid as a documented false positive of the paper's own detector: "It is not a curation defect ... the test-to-train similarity has a minimum of 0.707 and a median of 0.968 ... A near-duplicate leak fraction carries no information there."

suggested_fix: Either compute and commit the min/median similarity distribution for virus_covid so the numbers have a source, or drop them. Separately, split the reading: the Jaccard fraction of 1.000 is uninformative under conservation, but the 3.94% byte-identical rate is a real, conservation-independent finding and should be reported as such rather than absorbed into the false-positive concession.

claim: EDIT 3's headline: "the benchmark punishes the correct methodology -- the leakage-aware tuner's model appears 10.8 points worse on the as-shipped split (0.751 against 0.860) while in fact being 3.3 points better on the corrected one (0.729 against 0.696)."
defect: The 3.3-point corrected-split advantage carries no interval, and none exists anywhere in the repository. audit/experiments/exp_tuning.py computes acc_c as a single fit at a single split seed (SEED=0) and writes no bootstrap; tuning_selection.csv has no CI columns. This is a direct violation of the paper's own adjudication standard at main.tex:124, which requires that two models exchanging rank "each lead on their own split by a paired cluster-bootstrap difference whose interval excludes zero" precisely because the paper found bare point comparisons fire on clean controls. The 10.8-point half of the sentence is safe (0.8596 and 0.7513 are far apart); the 3.3-point half is the novel claim and is the one asserted without the machinery the paper elsewhere insists on. Available context suggests it is probably real but does not substitute for an interval: results/rf_seed_variance.csv shows msl=1 corrected accuracy varying 0.6957-0.7014 across five re-split seeds, so re-split variance alone consumes about a fifth of the 0.0334 gap, and exp_regpath.csv msl=50 (0.7278) sits within 0.0013 of msl=20 (0.7291), so the corrected-split optimum is flat. Note the comparison itself is fair on its face -- exp_tuning.py:98-99 fits both selected models on the same ctr and scores on the same cte -- so the objection is missing uncertainty, not an unfair contrast.
suggested_fix: Run a paired cluster-bootstrap on the corrected test set for msl=1 vs msl=20 (the same machinery already used for construction_manipulation.csv and the roster) and report the interval. If it excludes zero the claim stands as written; if not, weaken "3.3 points better" to "not worse", which still carries the argument.

claim: PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md EDIT 4a (staged for §4.9) and results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md:615 report that the eleven predicted-leaky GUE tasks are clean "with near-duplicate fractions spanning $0.005$--$0.041$ (median $0.009$)".

Truncating train can only lower a max-similarity-to-train statistic, so the quoted range and median are attenuated by roughly 2x. Full-scale recomputation gives a range of 0.009-0.041 with median 0.0136: the lower bound 0.005 does not exist at full scale and the median is understated by 51%. The verdicts survive (all remain far below the 0.1 cut), so the conclusion holds — but the numbers going into the manuscript do not, and this contradicts the paper's own practice recommendation at main.tex:378 ("Audit at full dataset scale, since subsampling can make a heavily leaky dataset look clean"). gue_census.csv also drops the verdict_is_lower_bound column that its predecessor results/crosssuite_census.csv carries for exactly this reason.
suggested_fix: Re-run the eleven predicted-leaky tasks at --cap 0 / full scale (each is seconds to ~20s), add verdict_is_lower_bound to gue_census.csv, and quote 0.009-0.041 (median 0.014) in EDIT 4a.

claim: EDIT 4(c) instructs: "Wherever the paper says Claim II 'requires short, fixed- or near-fixed-length human regulatory DNA' (Introduction, and the Discussion scope paragraph), that condition is now **refuted**". results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md:623-628 makes the same argument.
defect: This conflates two logically different statements. paper/main.tex:62 states a NECESSARY condition ("it is scoped: it requires both short, fixed- or near-fixed-length human regulatory DNA \emph{and} a memorization-prone model"). The GUE result — eleven short fixed-length human regulatory tasks that are clean — bears on a SUFFICIENCY claim, and is fully consistent with the necessary condition; clean tasks simply never reach the antecedent of Claim II. What GUE actually refutes is the pre-registration's §4.1 prediction that this regime would be leaky, which is a different proposition made in a different document. If EDIT 4(c) is merged as written the paper will (a) delete a true and defensible scope statement and (b) assert a refutation its own data does not license — a logic error a referee will catch immediately, and one that is worse than the stale text it replaces.
suggested_fix: Keep main.tex:62's necessary condition, and rewrite EDIT 4(a)/(c) to say GUE refutes the pre-registered expectation that the regime PREDICTS leakage — i.e. the regime is necessary but far from sufficient, and the discriminating factor is the un-deduplicated assembly step. Fix the parallel wording at TIER1_FINDINGS.md:623-628.

claim: The file contains two blocks both headed "## EDIT 3 — §5 Discussion". The first says "**Do not apply yet.** The ensembl tuning run is still going ... Until then the paragraph currently in §5 beginning *\"We report this for \textit{human\_nontata\_promoters} only\"* is accurate and should stay exactly as written."
defect: That HOLD block is stale and directly contradicts the resolved EDIT 3 twenty lines below it, which deletes the same paragraph as false. Since the parallel session is the sole owner of main.tex and works from this file, the stale instruction is the most likely proximate cause of the three blocker-level stale claims in main.tex surviving the merge — it explicitly tells the owner to leave the now-false paragraph alone.
suggested_fix: Delete the HOLD block outright and extend the status table to cover EDIT 4.

claim: §4 is headed "BINDING forward predictions (data not yet analysed locally)" and states "They are recorded before the corresponding experiments are run." The §4.1 GUE table carries no outcome.
defect: The GUE predictions have been executed and mostly failed. The document's own convention is to record outcomes inline rather than drop them — §0 does exactly that for the §1-A expectations ("Outcome of the §1-A expectations (recorded here rather than quietly dropped)") and §3 does it for R1-R6 ("Outcome: R1-R4 and R6 did not fire. R5 DID fire"). Leaving §4.1 as pending, with an 0/11 result recorded only in a separate findings file, is the one place in the repository where a failed pre-registered prediction is invisible from the registration itself.
suggested_fix: Append an outcome paragraph to §4.1 in the same style as §0's, stating 0/11 on the LEAKY row and the virus_covid false positive, and stating explicitly that mouse was never registered.

claim: "As of this session's last build, both disclosures are still true and correctly stated, and `PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md` did not yet exist", followed by a "## When the two jobs finish" section listing both merges as outstanding.
defect: Both jobs finished, both disclosures are now false, and PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md exists. The section also instructs "add the intervals to Table 2 (the manipulation table)" while the same file states four paragraphs earlier that "the manipulation table is **Table 4**" — an internal contradiction in the very document that governs the two-session merge. PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md EDIT 1 repeats the wrong number.
suggested_fix: Mark the handoff section closed and correct both "Table 2" references to Table 4 (tab:manip).

claim: EDIT 3 instructs the merger to "**Delete** the limitation sentence beginning *\"We report this for \textit{human\_nontata\_promoters} only\"* through *\"...does not yet establish it on the specific dataset carrying the reordering claim.\"*"
defect: Neither quoted anchor exists in main.tex. The file reads "We report **it** for \textit{human\_nontata\_promoters} only" and ends "and **not yet on** the specific dataset carrying the reordering claim". A mechanical find-and-replace merge will fail silently on both ends, leaving the false paragraph in place — the same failure mode as the stale HOLD block.
suggested_fix: Correct the two quoted anchors to the exact main.tex text.

claim: The module docstring declares "Out: results/gue_census.csv, results/gue_screen.csv" and describes STAGE 2 (the screen) as the stage that "matters", since it is what identifies candidate second-suite inversions.
defect: gue_screen.csv is never produced. The screen block is gated on `verdict != "clean" and len(np.unique(y)) == 2`; the only non-clean GUE task is virus_covid, which is 9-class, so the gate never fires and Stage 2 silently contributes nothing. Neither the log nor TIER1_FINDINGS §4.3 mentions that the stage the docstring calls decisive produced no output. Relatedly, results/gue_census.csv appears in no reproduction recipe: REPRODUCE.md's table has no exp_gue row, and results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md §6 lists six commands, none of them exp_gue or exp_tuning.
suggested_fix: State in §4.3 and the log that Stage 2 yielded zero candidate pairs (and why), and add exp_gue and exp_tuning rows to REPRODUCE.md and the TIER1_FINDINGS §6 block.

claim: "We report it for human_nontata_promoters only ... because the corresponding run on human_enhancers_ensembl exceeded our compute budget. It therefore establishes that leaky cross-validation selects the memorizing configuration on a leaky dataset, and not yet on the specific dataset carrying the reordering claim." And main.tex:124: "P5 fails outright."
defect: Both statements are invalidated by committed data. results/tuning_selection.csv now contains the human_enhancers_ensembl run (rows 2-3, committed in 3af3eb4), so the compute-budget disclaimer is false. Worse, that run REVERSES the paper's conclusion on the dataset that carries the reordering claim: on ensembl, naive CV selects min_samples_leaf=1 but grouped CV selects 20 -- i.e. P5 HOLDS there. The paper's bolded "Both select min_samples_leaf=1" and its Methods verdict "P5 fails outright" are therefore both wrong as global statements; P5 holds on one leaky dataset and fails on the other. The repo's own PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md EDIT 3 was written to fix exactly this and was never merged.
suggested_fix: Merge PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md EDIT 3 verbatim (its arithmetic checks out: 0.8596-0.7513=0.1083 -> 10.8 pts; 0.7291-0.6957=0.0334 -> 3.3 pts), and change main.tex:124 to "P5 holds on human_enhancers_ensembl and fails on human_nontata_promoters." Note the 3.3-point corrected-split advantage carries no interval; either add one or phrase it as a point estimate.

claim: "And each condition is a single fit at a single split seed with no interval attached, so we read the order-of-magnitude contrast against the control and not small differences between arms."
defect: False as of the committed data. results/construction_manipulation.csv now carries rf_drop_ci and lr_drop_ci on all six arms. Table 2 (main.tex:299-305) correspondingly omits the CI column. The paper is disclosing a limitation it no longer has, and the omission is not neutral: the intervals are disjoint between control and intervention in BOTH directions, which is the strongest form of the paper's only causal result. PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md EDIT 1 and EDIT 2 exist to fix this and were not merged.
suggested_fix: Merge PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md EDIT 1 and EDIT 2 as written; both are numerically correct against the CSV.

claim: gue_census.csv reports per-task leak fractions and clean/LEAKY verdicts as properties of the GUE tasks.
defect: exp_gue.py regresses a safeguard the repo already built and documented. The earlier census module records n_train_full/n_test_full alongside n_train_used/n_test_used plus an explicit verdict_is_lower_bound flag, precisely because train subsampling can only remove near-duplicate partners and therefore biases the leak fraction downward. exp_gue.py writes only n_train/n_test (the USED counts) with no full-size column and no lower-bound flag, so gue_census.csv states n_train=20000 for a task whose train set is 47,356. I recomputed at full train and the understatement is 2-3.7x on every capped task, and larger still against the pool a practitioner actually trains on (train+dev).
suggested_fix: Add n_train_full/n_test_full and verdict_is_lower_bound to exp_gue.py's row dict, mirroring exp_crosssuite_census.py, and rerun. The clean verdicts survive (all eleven stay far below the 0.1 cut even at full train+dev), so this costs nothing and closes the objection.

claim: emp_H3K4me3 leak_containment_0p7 = 0.0929, verdict = clean, prereg_correct = True.
defect: The verdict flips at full scale. main.tex:185 states the paper's own protocol -- "Because a k-mer Jaccard is length-capped, we re-measured at full scale with the length-robust containment index" -- and applies it to relabel demo_coding_vs_intergenomic_seqs from clean (Jaccard 0.078) to borderline (full-scale containment 0.131). exp_gue.py applies the 20,000 cap to the containment measure as well, and emp_H3K4me3's full-scale containment is 0.1375, above the same 0.1 cut. This is the identical situation the paper already ruled must escalate a verdict, and the census resolves it the other way. The 5/17 headline is unaffected (exp_gue.py:113-114 maps borderline to CLEAN), but the census's containment column as published is not the quantity the paper's protocol defines.
suggested_fix: Compute containment at full train scale for every GUE task (it is cheap -- the whole census ran in ~90s), and report emp_H3K4me3 as containment-borderline. Note the other two emp tasks are uncapped and sit at 0.0922/0.0821, so the cluster is genuinely near the threshold and should be described as such.

claim: "Leakage does not track task type: eleven independently built benchmarks in precisely the regime we flagged carry none of it."
defect: The eleven are not eleven, and are not independent of evidence the paper already reports. (i) Within GUE, prom_core_all's test set is EXACTLY the union of prom_core_notata's and prom_core_tata's -- zero set difference in either direction, sizes 5305+611=5916. The same holds for prom_300. So the six promoter tasks rest on two test sets, not six. (ii) Across suites, GUE's prom_300_* tasks share their sequence pool with the Nucleotide Transformer promoter tasks the paper already censused: 45% of GUE prom_300 train rows appear verbatim in NT promoter_all, and GUE's train+dev size (53,276) is exactly NT promoter_all's train size. So two of the remaining constructions re-measure evidence already in the paper. The honest count is at most ~7 distinct constructions (2 promoter window-widths x nested subsets, 5 TF datasets from one ENCODE pipeline), two of which duplicate the NT census. "Eleven independently built benchmarks" materially overstates the independent replication behind the scope-narrowing conclusion.
suggested_fix: Replace "eleven independently built benchmarks" with an accurate count and structure, e.g. "eleven GUE tasks spanning two promoter locus sets (at 70 and 300 bp, each partitioned into all/no-TATA/TATA) and five ENCODE transcription-factor datasets," and state explicitly that the 300 bp promoter tasks share ~45% of their rows with the NT promoter tasks already censused in this paper, so they are a consistency check rather than independent replication.

claim: "the test-to-train similarity has a minimum of 0.707 and a median of 0.968" for virus_covid.
defect: Neither number reproduces from the committed pipeline. Running the exact code path (exp_gue.py load_task with cap=20000, seed=0, then expkit.max_sim_to_train k=8 jaccard) gives min 0.7767 and median 0.9817. Nor can they come from a larger training pool: max-similarity is monotone non-decreasing in the train set, so the full 73,335-row train can only push both statistics UP, never down to 0.707/0.968. These are the two load-bearing numbers in the paper's proposed false-positive defense -- the whole "it is not a curation defect, the corpus is near-identical by biology" argument rests on them -- and they are not traceable to any committed artifact. gue_census.csv records only jac@0.7=1.0 and phi=0.999, which are consistent with but do not yield either figure.
suggested_fix: Add min/median/quantiles of sim_j to the census row dict in exp_gue.py so these are committed artifacts, and correct the paragraph to 0.777 and 0.982. Separately: the false-positive reading itself survives scrutiny -- the paper's own leaky datasets are backed by exact-duplicate and coordinate-space evidence that biology cannot produce (construction_manipulation.csv B_control exact_dup_test_in_train=0.3853; main.tex:289 coordinate separation 0.755/0.992 vs <=0.073), so the virus_covid argument does not undermine them. That defense should be stated in the limitation, not left implicit.

claim: "with near-duplicate fractions spanning 0.005--0.041 (median 0.009)" -- presented as a property of GUE's eleven predicted-leaky tasks.
defect: These are cap-suppressed measurements quoted as dataset properties. I confirmed the arithmetic reproduces the committed CSV (sorted: 0.0051,0.0053,0.0054,0.008,0.009,0.009,0.009,0.010,0.023,0.0277,0.0408 -> median 0.009, range 0.005-0.041), but eight of the eleven were measured on a 20,000-row subsample of a train set up to 2.4x larger. Recomputed at full train the range and median both shift materially; against train+dev, more so. The conclusion is unaffected -- every value stays far below the 0.1 cut -- but a reviewer who recomputes will get different numbers than the paper prints, which is exactly the failure mode this paper is about.
suggested_fix: Rerun the census uncapped (it costs seconds for these tasks) and quote the full-scale range and median, or state explicitly that the figures are subsample lower bounds.

claim: "Wherever the paper says Claim II 'requires short, fixed- or near-fixed-length human regulatory DNA' ... that condition is now refuted and should be replaced by the construction condition."
defect: Necessary-vs-sufficient error. main.tex:62 states the sequence-length condition as NECESSARY ("it requires both X and Y"). The GUE result is that eleven tasks satisfying X are clean -- which refutes the claim that X is SUFFICIENT, not that it is necessary. The pre-registration made a sufficiency-flavored forward prediction (short human regulatory => LEAKY) and that prediction failed; the paper's scope sentence is a different proposition and is untouched by the evidence. Acting on this instruction would delete a correctly hedged scope condition on the basis of a non sequitur, and would replace it with a construction condition that GUE cannot establish as necessary either (no GUE task was shown to have an un-deduplicated assembly AND be clean, nor the converse). The same slip appears at PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md:151 ("This refutes the scope hypothesis the prediction encoded") -- true of the pre-registration, false of main.tex:62.
suggested_fix: Keep the necessary-condition phrasing at main.tex:62. Report GUE as refuting the pre-registration's sufficiency prediction and as evidence that the construction step, not the task type, is what predicts leakage -- adding the construction condition alongside the length condition rather than replacing it.

claim: Module docstring: "Out: results/gue_census.csv, results/gue_screen.csv", with STAGE 2 (the inversion screen) described at lines 14-25 as the reason the module matters.
defect: results/gue_screen.csv does not exist and was never written. Stage 2 is gated at line 122 on `verdict != "clean" and len(np.unique(y)) == 2`. Sixteen tasks censused clean, so they skip it; the one LEAKY task, virus_covid, has n_classes=9, so it fails the binary guard. The screen therefore ran on zero tasks and main() line 168 skips the empty frame silently. The module's stated primary purpose produced nothing, and any downstream statement that GUE was screened for ranking inversions would be unsupported.
suggested_fix: Either extend the screen to multiclass (the delta/Dg condition does not require binary labels -- only expkit.correctness is used, which is multiclass-safe) so virus_covid is actually screened, or state in the docstring and any write-up that the screen was vacuous because no task met both gates.

claim: "Counting note: GUE ships train/dev/test. We use train as train and test as test, and ignore dev, so the split we audit is the one the leaderboard reports on."
defect: The justification does not follow. Reporting on test is a reason to keep test as the query set, not a reason to exclude dev from the reference set. Under GUE's own convention a model trains on train and selects on dev, so the practitioner's effective training pool is train+dev; leakage measured against train alone understates the contamination that practitioner induces. The effect is real but small, and it compounds with the 20,000 cap. Note also that the loader (lines 65-68) only ever downloads train and test, so the docstring's assertion about dev is not verified by the code that runs.
suggested_fix: Either fold dev into the reference set (one line in load_task) or restate the note as a deliberate lower-bound choice rather than a leaderboard-alignment argument.

claim: A single Jaccard>0.7 threshold at k=8 is applied uniformly across tasks whose median lengths span 70 to 999 bp, and the resulting clean verdicts on 70 bp tasks are read as evidence those tasks carry no near-duplicates.
defect: The threshold is not length-neutral, and the paper should say so. At 70 bp a sequence has ~63 8-mers and the Jaccard>0.7 cut admits at most ONE substitution -- it is effectively a step function, not a graded similarity. At 999 bp the same cut tolerates ~22 substitutions. In relative terms this is 1.4% divergence at 70 bp versus 2.2% at 999 bp, so the short human regulatory tasks the census clears are being held to a ~1.5x stricter near-duplicate definition than the 500 bp emp tasks and than the paper's own 251-269 bp datasets. This does not invalidate the clean verdicts, but it is an unstated asymmetry in exactly the comparison the GUE conclusion turns on.
suggested_fix: Disclose the length dependence in one sentence, and cite the available defense from the same table: prom_core_tata is 70 bp, uncapped, and the estimator fires there (jac@0.7=0.0408, exact_dup_test_in_train=0.0261), so the detector is demonstrably not floored at 70 bp -- the clean verdicts on the other short tasks are informative, not artifacts.

claim: REPRODUCE.md documents how to regenerate the repo's committed results.
defect: The GUE experiment is absent. grep for 'gue' across REPRODUCE.md, EXECUTION_PLAN.md and HANDOFF.md returns nothing, so results/gue_census.csv -- which the pending manuscript edits treat as load-bearing evidence for a scope change and a documented detector false positive -- has no reproduction entry. Every other experiment in audit/experiments/ that feeds a committed CSV is covered.
suggested_fix: Add the invocation (python -m audit.experiments.exp_gue), its runtime (~90s, dominated by virus_covid at 40s), the ~166 MB HF download, and note that results depend on the --cap value.

claim: §4.5 states the balanced graded gaps as "the linear models at the bottom ($+0.144$, $+0.139$)" and that naive Bayes's raw $-0.234$ becomes "$+0.141$".
defect: Two of these numbers contradict the paper's own Table 4 and the source CSV, and the qualitative ordering claim is false. Logistic regression's balanced gap is 0.1538 (Table 4 line 262 prints 0.154), not 0.139. GaussianNB's is 0.1289 (Table 4 line 264 prints 0.129), not 0.141. The text has swapped the two models' values. Consequently "the linear models at the bottom" is also wrong: GaussianNB at 0.129 sits below both linear models (0.144, 0.154), and kNN-15 at 0.016 is far below all three. The bottom of the roster is not the linear models.
suggested_fix: Change "($+0.144$, $+0.139$)" to "($+0.144$, $+0.154$)" and "$+0.016$ and $+0.141$" to "$+0.016$ and $+0.129$". Replace "with the linear models at the bottom" with a formulation that survives the data, e.g. "with the linear models, boosting and naive Bayes clustered between $+0.129$ and $+0.162$".

claim: "The memorizers average $+0.292$ against $+0.147$ for the rest" (human_enhancers_ensembl), and at :246/:276 "memorizers $+0.122$ against $+0.166$ for the rest/others, and the largest belongs to the MLP" (human_nontata_promoters).
defect: The comparison-group average silently excludes the MLP, so the two groups do not partition the nine-model roster — 4 memorizers + 4 "rest" = 8 of 9. Recomputing with the MLP in "the rest", which is where §4.4 line 242 explicitly places it ("it is not one of the four learners we designated memorization-prone in advance"), gives +0.165 not +0.147 on ensembl and +0.179 not +0.166 on nontata. The excluded model is the highest-gap non-memorizer on both datasets, so the omission inflates the separation the mechanism claim rests on. On nontata the sentence is self-contradictory on its face: it reports the largest of "the others" as belonging to the MLP while excluding the MLP from the others' mean.
suggested_fix: Recompute both contrasts over all five non-memorizers (+0.292 vs +0.165; +0.122 vs +0.179) and state the group membership explicitly, or keep the four-model comparison but name it ("against +0.147 for the four non-neural non-memorizers, the MLP excluded and reported separately at +0.234").

claim: "Two of the eleven are exact unions of two others (\textit{prom\_core\_all} is precisely \textit{prom\_core\_notata} $\cup$ \textit{prom\_core\_tata}, and likewise at $300$\,bp), so the independent count is nine test partitions rather than eleven."
defect: The exact-union relation holds only for the test partitions, not for the tasks. The training sets are not unions: prom_core_all's train set contains 5,205 sequences absent from prom_core_notata ∪ prom_core_tata, and the union contains 5,182 absent from it — roughly 11% divergence each way, with the same pattern at 300 bp. The `_all` task is a differently-drawn train/test partition of the same underlying pool whose test side happens to coincide exactly. Since the census's leak fraction is a test-to-train statistic, calling the task "precisely" the union overstates a dependence that is exact on one side only. The repo's own code states the narrower, correct claim; the manuscript generalized it.
suggested_fix: Restrict the parenthetical to the test side: "the \textit{\_all} tasks ship the exact union of the notata and tata \emph{test} partitions (zero symmetric difference), though their training sides differ by about 11%". The conservative count of nine is unaffected and can stand.

claim: §4.4 reports the P1 outcome as "the first depends on which form of the gap is used" — "Under the \emph{raw} gap it fails ... under the prevalence-corrected gap it holds decisively" — closing with "the prediction was made about memorization propensity, and the corrected statistic is the one that measures it."
defect: The Results treatment of P1 is materially softer than the Methods treatment of the same prediction, and it resolves in the authors' favour. Methods (:124) says flatly "P1 fails as registered", labels the corrected-gap result "post hoc", and states "we do not count this as a confirmation". §4.4 never uses the word "fails" for this dataset, never uses the phrase "post hoc", renders the verdict as a matter of which statistic one prefers, and then argues affirmatively that the post hoc statistic is the correct one. A reader of the Results section alone comes away with P1 confirmed. The structure compounds this: the balanced gap was defined after P1 was committed and after the registered statistic returned the wrong answer, yet Table 4 makes Gap_bal the bolded primary column and captions it "the statistic we rely on", demoting the registered statistic to a comparison column. The disclaimer lives in Methods; the credit is banked in Results and in the table. A hostile referee would accept the Methods paragraph and reject §4.4 as claiming a pre-registered win through a post hoc statistic — the exact selective-reporting pattern the paper elsewhere condemns.
suggested_fix: Open the §4.4 sentence with the Methods verdict verbatim — "P1 fails as registered" — and carry the post hoc label into the clause that reports the corrected-gap result, e.g. "under the prevalence-corrected gap, a statistic defined after P1 was committed, 1-NN does lead ($+0.461$ against $+0.319$); we report this as post hoc and do not score it as a confirmation." Delete or requalify "the corrected statistic is the one that measures it", which argues the prediction was right after conceding it was not.

claim: "all eleven predicted-leaky tasks are clean, with near-duplicate fractions from $0.011$ to $0.041$ under the $k$-mer Jaccard".
defect: The stated lower bound of the Jaccard range is wrong. The minimum over the eleven predicted-LEAKY tasks is 0.009 (human_tf_4), with human_tf_2 at 0.010 — two tasks fall below the stated 0.011. The containment range ("0.014 to 0.042") and both maxima are correct. The error is conservative in direction, but the range as printed is not the range in the data, and this is the sentence carrying the paper's headline failed-prediction result.

claim: "Two of the eleven are exact unions of two others ... so the independent count is nine test partitions rather than eleven" (l.331) and "nine independently built benchmarks in precisely the regime we flagged carry none of it" (l.333).
defect: The count of nine treats the 70 bp (prom_core_*) and 300 bp (prom_300_*) promoter families as independent. They are not: they are the same loci at two window widths, ~90% nested. Recomputed from the shipped files, 5337/5920 = 90.15% of prom_core_all test windows occur as exact substrings of the prom_300_all corpus (notata 4778/5307 = 90.03%, tata 552/613 = 90.05%); the reverse direction agrees at 5338/5920 = 90.17% of prom_300_all test sequences containing a prom_core window. Per-variant train/test row counts are also identical between the two families (all: 47356/5920; notata: 42452/5307; tata: 4904/613). The promoter families therefore contribute 2 independent test partitions, not 4, making the correct independent count SEVEN (2 promoter + 5 TF), not nine. Both the Results sentence and the Discussion's "independently built" restatement overstate the surviving evidence by 2/9.
suggested_fix: Change "nine" to "seven" at main.tex:331 and 333, and state that the 70 bp and 300 bp promoter families are nested (~90% substring overlap) rather than independent. Update N_INDEPENDENT_LEAKY_PREDICTIONS in audit/experiments/exp_gue.py:86 to 7.

claim: Code comment: "The 70 bp and 300 bp families are, by contrast, genuinely different windows: only 8% of the 70 bp test windows occur as substrings of the 300 bp corpus."
defect: The stated statistic is wrong by an order of magnitude and inverts its own conclusion. The true value is 90.15%, not 8%. No reading of the statistic reproduces 8%: against the 300 bp test set alone it is 10.52% (623/5920), against 300 bp train alone 80.61% (4772/5920), against the full corpus 90.15% (5337/5920). This false comment is the sole stated justification for treating the two promoter families as independent, and it is what sets N_INDEPENDENT_LEAKY_PREDICTIONS = 9 at line 86, which the paper then quotes. A committed artifact carries a verifiably false supporting measurement.
suggested_fix: Replace the comment with the measured 90.15% figure and the conclusion it actually supports (the families are nested, not independent), then propagate to N_INDEPENDENT_LEAKY_PREDICTIONS.

claim: "...with near-duplicate fractions from $0.011$ to $0.041$ under the $k$-mer Jaccard and $0.014$ to $0.042$ under containment".
defect: The stated Jaccard lower bound is wrong. Across the eleven predicted-LEAKY rows the minimum leak_jaccard_0p7 is 0.0090 (human_tf_4), and human_tf_2 is 0.0100 — both fall below the stated 0.011 floor. Two of eleven rows lie outside the range the paper reports as covering them. The containment range (0.0138 to 0.0424 -> "0.014 to 0.042") and the Jaccard maximum (0.0408 -> "0.041") are correct; only the Jaccard minimum is misstated.
suggested_fix: Change "from $0.011$ to $0.041$" to "from $0.009$ to $0.041$" at main.tex:331.

claim: T12: `python -m audit.experiments.exp_gue --cap 100000` produces `gue_census.csv`, `gue_screen.csv`.
defect: The documented command does not reproduce the shipped artifact. With no --tasks argument the run uses DEFAULT = list(PREREG) + list(EXPLORATORY) (exp_gue.py:73), which includes mouse_0 and mouse_1, yielding a 17-row gue_census.csv. The shipped results/gue_census.csv has 15 rows and exp_gue_full.log shows only 15 tasks censused, so the shipped run was invoked with an explicit --tasks list that REPRODUCE.md does not record. A reviewer following T12 gets a different artifact than the one committed.
suggested_fix: Either record the exact --tasks invocation used in REPRODUCE.md:94, or re-run with defaults so the shipped CSV matches the documented command.

claim: Code comment: mouse_0/mouse_1 "are censused and reported, separately and unscored"; main() carries a print block that reports exploratory verdicts and warns they must not be added to the registered tally.
defect: The commitment is not honoured by any shipped artifact. mouse_0 and mouse_1 appear in neither results/gue_census.csv nor exp_gue_full.log nor paper/main.tex (grep for "mouse" in main.tex returns nothing). Removing the rows entirely rather than keeping them flagged registered=False loses real information: the only surviving mouse census is the superseded capped run, where mouse_1 was truncated 53952 -> 20000, i.e. its clean verdict there IS a lower bound. There is now no full-scale mouse census anywhere in the repo, and the exploratory print path at lines 236-241 is dead code that never fired.
suggested_fix: Re-run the two exploratory tasks at full scale and keep them in gue_census.csv with registered=False (they are already excluded from the tally by the registered flag), rather than deleting the rows.

claim: "\textit{prom\_core\_all} is precisely \textit{prom\_core\_notata} $\cup$ \textit{prom\_core\_tata}, and likewise at $300$\,bp".
defect: Stated without qualification about the dataset, but it holds only for the test splits. For the train splits the union is not exact: prom_core_all.train has 5205 sequences absent from notata+tata train and the union has 5182 absent from all.train (of 47356). Same at 300 bp (5234 / 5228). The code comment at exp_gue.py:76-78 correctly scopes the claim to .test; the paper drops the scope. The downstream conclusion ("nine test partitions") is scoped correctly, so only the sentence as written is wrong, not the inference it supports.
suggested_fix: Qualify to the test splits, e.g. "the test split of prom_core_all is precisely the union of the prom_core_notata and prom_core_tata test splits".

claim: "\textit{emp\_H3K4me3} ... has a containment leak fraction of $0.137$ at full scale against $0.093$ on a capped run".
defect: 0.1375 rounds to 0.138, not 0.137. The capped figure 0.0929 -> 0.093 is correct. Rounding direction is inconsistent between the two numbers in the same sentence.

claim: The future-work sentence names DeepSTARR, BEND and DART-Eval as "the obvious next targets" on the explicit basis that "each assembles its examples from genome-tiled or annotation-overlapping intervals, which is the construction step that produced the defect here", and closes "That is a prediction about how a dataset was built ... and it is the one our evidence actually supports."
defect: The stated basis is unverified in the repo and is a non-sequitur for all three named benchmarks, each of which ships chromosome-disjoint splits -- the very control this paper uses to validate its own findings (sec:chrom). BEND partitions samples by chromosome and additionally partitions gene finding at 80% identity; DART-Eval fixes test = chr 5,10,14,18,20,22 and validation = chr 6,21; DeepSTARR holds out chr2R entirely. Genome-tiled assembly plus a chromosome-disjoint split does not reproduce the Genomic Benchmarks defect, which arose from a random split over an un-deduplicated interval pool drawn from the same chromosomes. The sentence is framed as the careful replacement for the falsified GUE pre-registration ("We state the basis for that expectation carefully, having just had the same expectation falsified"), so an unsupported and contradicted premise here is materially misleading. It is also internally inconsistent: the paper cites teufel2023graphpart at main.tex:130 as the reference whole-cluster partitioner, whose first author is a BEND co-author.
suggested_fix: Either drop the construction premise and state the three benchmarks as untested targets without a predicted verdict, or replace it with the accurate observation that all three already apply chromosome-disjoint (and in BEND's case identity-based) partitioning, and reframe the open question as whether chromosome disjointness is sufficient to remove near-duplicate leakage -- which is a question this paper's own chromosome-holdout control (sec:chrom, which "leaves a small residual") is positioned to ask.

claim: Defending the C9 cohesion cut, which is calibrated on only two datasets: "The cut is calibrated on the two leaky datasets studied here, which fall an order of magnitude either side of it: human_enhancers_ensembl has cohesion 0.96 and human_nontata_promoters 0.08."
defect: "an order of magnitude either side of it" is false on the upper side. With the cut at 0.5, human_enhancers_ensembl's 0.9586 is 1.92x the cut, not 10x; only human_nontata_promoters (0.083, 6.0x below) is anywhere near an order of magnitude away, and neither is a full decade. Cohesion is bounded above by 1.0, so no dataset can ever sit an order of magnitude above a 0.5 cut -- the claim is unachievable by construction. This is the single sentence in the paper that justifies stating a hand-set threshold in the literature on an n=2 calibration, and it overstates the calibration margin by roughly 5x on the side where the cut is least constrained (any cut in (0.084, 0.958] would separate these two datasets identically).
suggested_fix: Replace with the accurate statement, e.g. "the two leaky datasets studied here differ by more than a factor of ten in cohesion (0.96 vs 0.08) and any cut between them separates them identically; we set it at 0.5 as a midpoint and note that a two-dataset calibration fixes only the order of magnitude, not the value."

claim: The scope sentence states "\S\ref{sec:r-census} reports eleven benchmarks in exactly that regime, pre-registered by us as leaky, that are clean", and main.tex:386 repeats "eleven GUE tasks meeting exactly that description are clean". The abstract (main.tex:49) says "all eleven are clean".
defect: The paper's own results section states the correct independent count as nine: main.tex:333 says "nine independently built benchmarks in precisely the regime we flagged carry none of it". Two of the eleven are exact unions of two others, so the eleven are not eleven independent observations. The larger, weaker-per-unit number is used in the three load-bearing rhetorical positions (abstract, scope statement, future-work justification) while the correct deduction appears only in the results narrative, without either location cross-referencing the other. A reader of the scope sentence takes the falsification of the pre-registration to rest on eleven independent benchmarks.
suggested_fix: Use the same qualification everywhere: "eleven tasks (nine independently built; prom_core_all and prom_300_all are exact unions of their notata and tata components)", and carry the parenthetical into the abstract and both Discussion sentences.

claim: The paper defines the certified quantity exactly: cluster cohesion is "the fraction of its $\binom{m}{2}$ member pairs that actually exceed the similarity threshold", and main.tex:379 repeats "the fraction of member pairs in the largest near-duplicate component that are genuine edges".
defect: certify.py does not compute this quantity for any component larger than 300 members; it draws a deterministic 300-member subsample and reports an estimate. The tool records this in a JSON field the paper never mentions, so a reader who runs certify on their own dataset and gets a cohesion near the 0.5 cut has no way to know from the paper that the number is a sampling estimate with error, not the defined statistic. On this repo's own chained dataset (largest component 420 members) the tool already reports 0.0835 against the exact 0.083 computed by exp_geometry G11, i.e. the two published paths for the same number disagree in the third decimal for an undisclosed reason. The manuscript's C9 discussion presents a single number as though one estimator produced it.
suggested_fix: Add one clause to main.tex:158 or :379 stating that the tool enumerates all pairs up to a 300-member component and reports an unbiased subsample estimate above that, and hoist the `cohesion_estimated_on_subsample` assignment out of the `if nm > 1` block at certify.py:336 so the key is always present.

claim: Section 4.1 is titled "Leakage is dataset-specific and clean verdicts survive a length-robust re-measure", and the report card (Table tab:reportcard) issues human_ensembl_regulatory the verdict "clean" with an unexplained "--" in the leak@0.7 (con) column. main.tex:187 states "the three-class human_ensembl_regulatory set is likewise clean (0.005)".
defect: One of the six clean verdicts was never subjected to the length-robust check the section title advertises, and the table's "--" is not defined in the caption while every other cell is. This matters because containment is precisely what flipped demo_coding_vs_intergenomic_seqs from clean to borderline in the same table -- the paper's own evidence that a Jaccard-only clean verdict is unreliable. The tool inherits the gap silently: --self-validate reads the containment as NaN, and because NaN > 0.1 is False, verdict_from returns "clean" and the C2 check reports "pass" rather than flagging the measurement as unavailable -- the same inert-check failure mode the tool deliberately guards against for C1 (which returns UNVERIFIABLE and downgrades to provisional-clean).
suggested_fix: Define "--" in the table caption as "containment not measured" and mark that verdict as clean (Jaccard only), or measure containment for the 3-class set. In certify.py, make verdict_from and the C2 check treat a NaN containment as UNVERIFIABLE rather than as a pass, mirroring the C1 treatment.

claim: The --emit-splits payload is written with both key spellings under the inline comment "both spellings, so this file loads into either tool without a shim", and the --emit-splits help text at certify.py:480-484 advertises "certify then retrain" composition.
defect: There is no second tool that reads a split file. audit/core/homology_split.py is write-only: its CLI takes --fasta/--labels and emits splits.json, and it contains no json.load and no split-reading code path. The dual-spelling payload therefore composes only with certify's own --splits flag (which I confirmed round-trips), so "either tool" names a consumer that does not exist. The reverse direction claimed in the module docstring (certify.py:51-52, "a split written by audit/core/homology_split.py loads directly") is real and verified.
suggested_fix: Reword the comment and help text to name the actual consumer ("loads back into certify --splits, and matches the key spelling homology_split.py emits"), or add a --splits input path to homology_split.py so the advertised round trip exists.

claim: "Drawing random pairs from the datasets we certify clean [...] individual unrelated pairs do reach a Jaccard of $0.26$, far above the $0.019$ maximum seen on synthetic sequence."
defect: The real-DNA floor is measured on only three datasets whose median lengths are 316, 2143 and 500 bp. It contains no measurement at 70 bp or 101 bp -- the exact regimes the surrounding paragraph is about ("a 70 bp sequence holds only 63 k-mers"; "at 70 bp it already misses two point mutations 70% of the time") and the regimes of the eleven predicted-leaky GUE tasks the calibration exists to defend. Short sequences are where the k-mer set is smallest and the background tail is worst-behaved, so the omitted regime is the one where the null is least favourable. The quoted 0.26 consequently understates the real-DNA extreme at the lengths that carry the claim.
suggested_fix: Add prom_core_all (70 bp) and human_tf_0 (101 bp) to real_dna_floor()'s dataset list (audit/experiments/exp_estimator_sensitivity.py:152) and requote the extreme from the short-length rows, or restrict the sentence to the >=300 bp regime actually measured.

claim: "But not one of $12{,}000$ such pairs reaches the operating threshold of $0.7$, so the false-positive rate at the threshold we actually use is zero on real DNA as well as synthetic, and the measured leak fractions are not noise."
defect: The pair count is roughly three orders of magnitude too small to support the inference. The census statistic is not a per-pair rate: for each test sequence it takes a maximum over all n_train training sequences, so the per-pair false-positive rate must be far below 1/n_train for the floor to be negligible. Observing 0 of 11,998 bounds the per-pair rate only at 3/11,998 = 2.5e-4 by the rule of three; propagated through prom_core_all's n_train = 47,356 that admits a noise-only leak fraction of 1-(1-2.5e-4)^47356 = 0.9999. The experiment is therefore consistent with the measured leak fractions being entirely noise, which is the opposite of what the sentence asserts. Supporting a noise-only leak fraction below 0.01 at that n_train needs a per-pair bound of ~2.1e-7, i.e. on the order of 1.4e7 pairs.
suggested_fix: Either raise n_pairs to ~1e7 (cheap: the pair loop is the only cost) and quote the resulting bound propagated through n_train, or drop "the measured leak fractions are not noise" and state only the weaker supported claim, that no real unrelated pair was observed near the threshold.

claim: "the false-positive rate at the threshold we actually use is zero on real DNA as well as synthetic" -- immediately followed by "The containment index is also uniformly the more sensitive of the two metrics at short length, which is why we report both rather than treat the second as redundant."
defect: real_dna_floor() computes Jaccard only; containment is never evaluated on real DNA, and results/estimator_specificity_real.csv has no containment column. But containment at 0.7 is one of "the threshold[s] we actually use": it is a reported census column (leak_containment_0p7) and it is the metric that produces the one verdict change the paper highlights (emp_H3K4me3, 0.1375). The synthetic specificity run does report containment, so the omission is specific to the real-DNA arm -- i.e. exactly the arm where the paper says the null matters. The generalisation to "the threshold we actually use" is therefore unsupported for the more sensitive of the two metrics, and containment's higher sensitivity (asserted in the very next sentence) makes it the metric more likely to have a nonzero real-DNA floor.
suggested_fix: Compute containment alongside Jaccard in real_dna_floor() and add containment_max / containment_fp_rate columns, then requote; or narrow the sentence to the 8-mer Jaccard explicitly.

claim: "Drawing random pairs from the datasets we certify clean---where any similarity between two members is, by that verdict, not leakage---" (and the identical docstring justification at exp_estimator_sensitivity.py:146-149).
defect: The identifying assumption is false as stated. A "clean" verdict means only that the near-duplicate leak fraction falls below the 0.1 cut, not that it is zero; the certified-clean datasets used here carry nonzero measured leakage. Any pair drawn from them that exceeded 0.7 would therefore most likely be genuine leakage counted as a false positive, and the reported zero is a mixture statistic, not a false-positive rate. This does not overturn the result -- random pair sampling almost never hits a duplicate partner when the test-side leak fraction is a few percent -- but the stated warrant for calling the measurement a false-positive floor does not hold.
suggested_fix: Replace the parenthetical with an explicit statement that these datasets carry small but nonzero measured leakage, so the quantity is an upper bound on the false-positive rate rather than a clean estimate of it.

claim: Table row T13: `python -m audit.experiments.exp_estimator_sensitivity` produces `estimator_{sensitivity,specificity,specificity_real}.csv`.
defect: The documented command does not reproduce the committed CSVs. argparse defaults --trials to 300 (exp_estimator_sensitivity.py:190), but the committed artefacts were generated at 200 trials. Following REPRODUCE.md verbatim silently overwrites the shipped results with different numbers, including the 0.019 synthetic maximum the paper quotes.
suggested_fix: Change the T13 command to `... exp_estimator_sensitivity --trials 200`, or change the argparse default to 200.

claim: Docstring: "The maximum over many such pairs is the false-positive floor: leak fractions comfortably above it are signal." Stdout: "The false-positive floor is far below the 0.1 verdict cut at every length, so measured leak fractions are not noise."
defect: Unit conflation retained in the module after it was removed from the manuscript. Both sentences compare a Jaccard similarity score (max ~0.019) against a leak fraction (the 0.1 verdict cut). These are different quantities in different units -- one is a per-pair similarity, the other a fraction of test sequences -- and being "above" a max-Jaccard value says nothing about whether a leak fraction is signal. The correct comparison for the similarity score is against the 0.7 operating threshold. The paper text no longer contains this, but a reproducer running the module reads it as the module's own conclusion.
suggested_fix: Reword both to compare 0.019 against the 0.7 operating threshold, and state the leak-fraction implication via the per-pair rate propagated through n_train.

claim: "not one of $12{,}000$ such pairs"
defect: Rounded up from the actual count. Self-collision rejection (`if i != j`) drops one pair in two of the three datasets, so the realised total is 11,998. Immaterial to the argument but inconsistent with the shipped CSV a referee would check.

claim: "across the fourteen clean GUE tasks, whose training sets run to $47{,}356$ sequences, $0.009$ to $0.041$" — the rebuilt specificity argument's GUE arm.
defect: There are fifteen clean GUE tasks in the shipped census, not fourteen. The only way to reach fourteen with a max n_train of 47,356 is the set {11 predicted-leaky} ∪ {emp_H3, emp_H3K4me3, emp_H4} — which (a) includes emp_H3K4me3, a task main.tex:335 explicitly reclassifies as "borderline rather than clean", and (b) silently drops mouse_0 and mouse_1, which ARE clean. The same sentence applies the opposite rule to Genomic Benchmarks, correctly excluding the borderline demo_coding to get "five clean". One sentence, two contradictory definitions of clean.
suggested_fix: State the set explicitly and apply one rule. Either "the thirteen clean GUE tasks excluding the two mouse tasks" (range 0.009–0.041), or include mouse and say "the fifteen clean GUE tasks" (range 0.000–0.041, which strengthens the floor argument). Do not count emp_H3K4me3 as clean here while calling it borderline in §4.3.

claim: The specificity argument rests on the estimator's reading "across the fourteen clean GUE tasks" as fourteen independent low readings establishing an estimator floor.
defect: The paper applies independence-deflation to its failed pre-registered arm (11 → 7, main.tex:331) but not to the arm that supports its estimator or to its only correct predictions. The three yeast EMP tasks are not three independent corpora — they are largely the same yeast sequences relabelled for different histone marks. emp_H3 and emp_H4 in particular share 6,043 sequences with identical labels on 94.3% of them. Under the paper's own §4.3 standard the fourteen collapse to roughly eight independent corpora (7 promoter/TF + ~1 yeast). The same inflation affects "the registered predictions score 3 of 15" (main.tex:331): the three correct predictions are, per results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md:658, "all yeast EMP" — i.e. one corpus counted three times.
suggested_fix: Apply the §4.3 independence lens symmetrically: report the specificity range over the independent corpora (~8, or state "fourteen task partitions spanning roughly eight independent corpora"), and add the same qualifier to "3 of 15" noting the three correct calls are one yeast corpus under three histone-mark labels.

claim: "The \textit{\_all} promoter tasks are the exact union of their own \textit{notata} and \textit{tata} variants, with empty symmetric difference"
defect: True for the test splits only; false for train, where the symmetric difference is ~11%. The paper states it unconditionally for "the tasks". Worse, ~5,231 sequences in prom_300_all's train appear nowhere in prom_300_notata or prom_300_tata across any split, so _all is not even a superset — the families each withhold a different ~10% (their unshipped dev partitions). The audit code gets this right and the paper dropped the scoping: audit/experiments/exp_gue.py:85 correctly writes "set(prom_core_all.test) = set(prom_core_notata.test) | set(prom_core_tata.test), symmetric difference zero".
suggested_fix: Scope the sentence to test, matching the code and matching the conclusion the paper actually draws: "The \_all promoter tasks' test sets are the exact union of their notata and tata test sets, with empty symmetric difference (the train sets are not — each family withholds a different ~10% as an unshipped dev partition)." The seven-test-partition count is unaffected.

claim: "likewise at 300 bp, so the independent count is **nine** test partitions." Same stale figure at results/tier1_preregistration.md:156; PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md:183 still says "a direct test on eleven independent benchmarks."
defect: Round 9's correction (eleven → nine → seven) landed in paper/main.tex and audit/experiments/exp_gue.py but not in the shipped narrative record. HANDOFF.md:58 designates results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md as the project's "Narrative" record and results/audit_findings.csv as the full one, so a reviewer following the repo hits nine where the paper says seven. The stale derivation is also the superseded one: it collapses only the _all = notata ∪ tata nesting and misses the 70bp/300bp same-loci nesting that takes nine to seven.
suggested_fix: Update results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md:632 and results/tier1_preregistration.md:156 to seven, adding the 70bp/300bp same-loci nesting to the derivation; fix PENDING_PARAGRAPHS.md:183 to "seven independent benchmarks" (the LaTeX block it proposes at lines 185-192 already needs the same edit — it says "Eleven GUE tasks in precisely that regime", where main.tex:62 and :397 correctly append "seven of them independent").

claim: Methods states the break-a-clean arm is built "by duplicating positives until the same 94.3% share of positive rows sits on a multiplicity-2 coordinate as we measure on human_enhancers_ensembl (which requires duplicating 89.1% of them ...), then downsampling to the control's exact size and class balance."
defect: The primary (size- and balance-matched) arm does not carry a 94.3% share. The downsample is not share-preserving: it keeps 10,000 of 18,914 positives, so ~47% of the manufactured duplicate pairs lose a partner and revert to multiplicity 1. Recomputing the realized share directly from audit/experiments/exp_dose_response.py:one_dose (identical construction to exp_construction_manip.py:145-170) gives 0.4986, not 0.9426 — a factor of 1.89. The same defect makes every dose label in §4.13 nominal rather than realized. The scientific conclusion is unaffected (the syndrome is in fact manufactured at half the advertised dose, which is stronger), but the reader is told the intervention is calibrated to the ensembl signature when the arm actually evaluated is not.
suggested_fix: Reword line 164 to state the share is imposed before matching and report the post-matching realized share (0.499). In §4.13 (paper/main.tex:340) define "dose" as the pre-matching target share and give the realized share alongside phi, or relabel the doses by realized share.

claim: Section title "A dose-response test: the condition predicts where the ranking flips", and line 338: "the condition makes a quantitative prediction about the dose at which the ranking should flip"; line 344: "What the experiment establishes is the positive arm, causally and at ten doses."
defect: The experiment does not locate the flip point. phi* is recomputed from scratch at every dose from that dose's own as-shipped strata, and is non-monotone across doses, varying nearly sevenfold. No single value of phi separates the inverting from the non-inverting arms: phi at the highest NON-inverting dose (0.25) is 0.0932, which exceeds phi* measured at all seven of the inverting doses, including the 0.0602 that line 342 quotes as "a predicted breakdown point" for the first inversion. Substituting the dose-0.30 phi* into the dose-0.25 arm predicts an inversion that does not occur. What the design supports is per-arm classification, not prediction of the flip dose. Separately, line 344's own accounting is inconsistent: it concedes that all three negatives are of the no-valid-challenger kind, then credits the positive arm with "ten doses" — only the seven doses with finite phi* bear on the positive arm.
suggested_fix: Retitle to what is tested (e.g. "the condition classifies each dose correctly") and replace "predicts the dose at which the ranking should flip" with the per-arm formulation. Note explicitly that phi* is re-measured at each dose and is not a fixed threshold locating the flip. Change "the positive arm, causally and at ten doses" to seven doses.

claim: REPRODUCE.md lists T1-T13 as the commands that regenerate the committed results, and the paper's Reproducibility subsection (paper/main.tex:177) presents the release as re-runnable.
defect: The dose-response module — the paper's newest headline experiment, carrying P6 and the claim "the condition is right on all ten doses" — has no entry in the reproduction table, and no documented command regenerates the shipped CSV. audit/experiments/exp_dose_response.py:64 defaults to six doses [0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9426]; the committed ten-row results/dose_response.csv was produced by a second, undocumented invocation with --doses 0.25 0.30 0.35 0.45 (exp_dose_fine.log) and a manual merge that is recorded nowhere. Worse, main() writes unconditionally to results/dose_response.csv (lines 164-166), so any re-run — including the documented-style default — silently replaces the merged ten-dose file with a six-dose (or smaller) subset. I hit this: re-running two doses truncated the committed CSV to two rows and I had to restore it from git.
suggested_fix: Add a T14 row to REPRODUCE.md giving the exact dose list that reproduces the committed CSV in one invocation (make DOSES the full ten), and either make the writer merge-by-dose or write to a run-specific filename so a partial run cannot clobber the shipped table.

claim: The rebuilt specificity argument: "across the fourteen clean GUE tasks, whose training sets run to 47,356 sequences, 0.009 to 0.041".
defect: There are thirteen GUE tasks the paper itself verdicts clean, not fourteen. The count of fourteen is the fifteen registered tasks minus virus_covid, which silently readmits emp_H3K4me3 — the task line 335 explicitly relabels "borderline rather than clean" on the strength of a 0.137 full-scale containment leak fraction. Since the whole point of the paragraph is what the estimator reads on data believed clean on independent grounds, including a task the paper has just declared possibly leaky weakens the argument it is meant to support.
suggested_fix: Change "fourteen clean GUE tasks" to thirteen and exclude emp_H3K4me3, or state that the count includes the one borderline task and that its Jaccard reading (0.0171) sits inside the quoted range.

claim: "We report instead what the statistic itself reads on data believed clean on independent grounds ... across the fourteen clean GUE tasks, whose training sets run to 47,356 sequences, 0.009 to 0.041."
defect: The GUE half of the rebuilt specificity argument is circular. No GUE task has any independent cleanliness evidence anywhere in the repo. The only artifact containing GUE task data is results/gue_census.csv, which is this estimator's own output, and 'clean' there is *defined* by the estimator: audit/experiments/exp_gue.py:158-159 sets verdict = LEAKY if jac07 > LEAK_CUT else borderline if con07 > LEAK_CUT else clean, with LEAK_CUT = 0.1 (line 49). So the sample over which the 0.041 maximum is taken is, by the selection rule, exactly the set of tasks on which the statistic read below 0.1. The subsequent conclusion ('the floor of this estimator ... is an order of magnitude below the verdict cut') is guaranteed by construction, not measured. The Genomic Benchmarks half of the same sentence is NOT circular -- results/construction_provenance.csv gives independent coordinate-space grounds for each of those five (documented merge/dedup step, R_self, frac_rows_on_dup_coord = 0) -- but both halves are presented under the single banner 'believed clean on independent grounds', which is false for the GUE half.
suggested_fix: Two non-circular replacements, both already computable from shipped data. (1) Anchor the floor on cleanliness established BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by verdict: results/construction_manipulation.csv row B_manipulated_merged_balanced reads leak_jaccard_0p7 = 0.0115 on n = 81,868 where every duplicated coordinate was collapsed by the intervention itself -- cleanliness there is a property of the edit, not of the estimator. The dose-0 control (results/dose_response.csv, 0.0005 on n = 20,000) is the same kind of datapoint. (2) For the GUE tasks, cite the one genuinely independent column in the census: exact_dup_test_in_train (0.000-0.026 across the eleven), which is computed by set membership on raw strings, no k-mers, a different code path from the Jaccard statistic. Then restate the sentence as 'across GB datasets independently established clean from their coordinates it reads 0.001-0.016; on GUE we can only report that the k-mer statistic and an independent exact-duplicate check agree, which is corroboration rather than an independent floor.'

claim: "The floor of this estimator on real DNA at realistic training-set size is therefore an order of magnitude below the verdict cut and more than twenty times below the leaky readings, which is the comparison the verdicts actually rest on."
defect: The sentence takes its safety margin from the minimum of the quoted range while the verdict rule's soundness depends on the maximum. At the 'realistic training-set size' the sentence explicitly names (the GUE tasks, up to 47,356 train rows) the largest clean reading is 0.041, which is 2.4x below the 0.1 verdict cut -- not an order of magnitude -- and 9.4x below the 0.384 leaky reading -- not 'more than twenty times'. The >20x figure only holds for the Genomic Benchmarks maximum (0.384 / 0.016 = 24), i.e. the set that is NOT at the realistic training-set size being invoked. As written, the concluding sentence is contradicted by the numbers in the sentence immediately preceding it.
suggested_fix: State the worst case explicitly: 'the largest reading on data we believe clean is 0.041, a factor 2.4 below the verdict cut and 9.4 below the leaky readings.' If the order-of-magnitude framing is kept, scope it to the Genomic Benchmarks set where it is true and say so.

claim: "The condition is right on all ten doses ... The ranking first inverts at dose 0.30, where phi = 0.106 against a predicted breakdown point of phi* = 0.060."
defect: The dose section omits the trivial-baseline comparison that Section 4.12 performs on the weaker GUE result, and that comparison would show phi* contributes nothing here. Two predictors with no phi*, no novel-stratum accuracies and no graded gaps also score 10/10 on the same rows: (a) 'invert iff the random forest leads the as-shipped split' -- rf_rank_orig is 4,4,3,1,1,1,1,1,1,1 against ranking_inverts F,F,F,T,T,T,T,T,T,T, an exact match; (b) any single fixed threshold on phi in the interval (0.0932, 0.1055), since phi is monotone in dose. The paper is scrupulous about this exact issue for GUE ('a constant "nothing swaps" predictor scores 23 of 24 on the same data, so all but two of the twenty-four opportunities are vacuous by construction', line 325) and applies no equivalent check to what it calls the sharper test. This is a different point from the limitation the section does disclose at line 344 (that the three negatives are of the no-valid-challenger kind): even on the positive arm the numeric value of phi* is never load-bearing, and phi* is non-monotone across doses (0.0602, 0.0554, 0.0375, 0.0803, 0.0116, 0.0612, 0.0212) so it locates no flip point.
suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Section 4.13 in the same form used at line 325: report that 'invert iff the forest leads as shipped' and a single fixed phi threshold each also score 10/10, so what the experiment establishes causally is that raising phi promotes the memorizer to as-shipped leader and that the corrected split reverses it -- not that phi* locates the flip dose. Drop or soften 'the condition makes a quantitative prediction about the dose at which the ranking should flip' (line 338), since phi* is undefined at every pre-flip dose and therefore predicted no dose.

claim: REPRODUCE.md's table T1-T13 is the reproduction path for the new experiments; the paper's Section 4.13 rests on results/dose_response.csv.
defect: exp_dose_response.py -- the paper's newest and most load-bearing experiment -- has no entry in REPRODUCE.md at all, and the shipped 10-row CSV cannot be regenerated by any documented command. The module's default DOSES list holds only six values (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9426); the other four (0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.45) came from a second invocation recorded only in exp_dose_fine.log. main() writes the current invocation's rows straight over the file with no merge -- unlike exp_construction_manip.py's --only merge, and unlike the merge-by-task fix just applied to exp_gue.py -- so running the module as shipped both destroys the 10-row file and yields a 6-dose result whose first inversion is at dose 0.40 (phi = 0.131, phi* = 0.038), not the dose 0.30 (phi = 0.106, phi* = 0.060) the paper reports.
suggested_fix: Add a T14 row to REPRODUCE.md with the explicit ten-dose invocation (--doses 0.0 0.2 0.25 0.3 0.35 0.4 0.45 0.6 0.75 0.9426, ~21 min), and give exp_dose_response.py the same merge-by-key logic exp_gue.py just received, keyed on dose_target_share, so a partial re-run cannot silently discard the rest of the grid.

claim: "The correction also disposes of two values the raw statistic produced that were never interpretable as memorization at all: 15-nearest-neighbour's raw -0.684 and naive Bayes's -0.234 become +0.016 and +0.141."
defect: Naive Bayes's corrected gap on human_enhancers_ensembl is +0.129, not +0.141, and the same paragraph already states it correctly two clauses earlier ('naive Bayes (+0.129)'). The paragraph therefore reports two different values for the same quantity. 0.1410 is the human_nontata_promoters value, pulled into a passage that is otherwise entirely about human_enhancers_ensembl.

claim: "across the fourteen clean GUE tasks, whose training sets run to 47,356 sequences, 0.009 to 0.041"
defect: The task count does not match the census in any state. At commit 8c2c49e, the commit that wrote this sentence, gue_census.csv held 13 tasks with verdict 'clean' (emp_H3, emp_H4, the five human_tf, and the six promoter tasks), plus emp_H3K4me3 at 'borderline' and virus_covid at 'LEAKY'. The quoted range 0.009-0.041 is exactly the min/max over those 13 (0.0087 emp_H3 to 0.0408 prom_core_tata), so the range is right and the count should read thirteen. In the current working tree the two mouse tasks have been censused and the clean count is 15, for which the range would start at 0.000 (mouse_0 = 0.0000). Fourteen matches neither; it would only be reached by counting emp_H3K4me3 as clean, which Section 4.12 explicitly declines to do.
suggested_fix: Say 'thirteen' and keep 0.009-0.041, or say 'fifteen' and widen the range to 0.000-0.041 while noting the two mouse tasks are unregistered exploratory additions.

claim: "Three of twelve Nucleotide Transformer tasks are similarly leaky" (abstract; repeated at :71 "three of twelve independent tasks", :322 "Counting independent tasks, three of twelve", :403 conclusion).
defect: Twelve is an overcount by the paper's own collapsing rule. §4.10 collapses GUE's prom_*_all because it is "the exact union of their own notata and tata variants, with empty symmetric difference". NT-original's promoter_all satisfies that criterion exactly and was not collapsed. §3.12 declares only one NT convention (enhancers ≡ enhancers_types), so the rule established in Round 9 was never back-applied to the suite where the count first appears.
suggested_fix: Change twelve to eleven at main.tex:49, :71, :322, :403, and state the second NT collapse in §3.12 alongside the enhancers/enhancers_types one. The leaky numerator (3) is unaffected.

claim: "across the fourteen clean GUE tasks, whose training sets run to 47,356 sequences, 0.009 to 0.041".
defect: Direct contradiction with §4.10, which reclassifies emp_H3K4me3 as borderline and says so explicitly: "emp_H3K4me3, registered clean, has a containment leak fraction of 0.137 at full scale ... which makes it borderline rather than clean." Only thirteen registered GUE tasks are clean. Including a task the paper has just declared borderline inside the reference set used to establish the estimator's clean-data floor is the wrong direction of error for a specificity argument.
suggested_fix: "thirteen clean GUE tasks", and either exclude emp_H3K4me3's reading from the quoted range or name it as the borderline task and report it separately.

claim: "The floor of this estimator on real DNA at realistic training-set size is therefore an order of magnitude below the verdict cut and more than twenty times below the leaky readings, which is the comparison the verdicts actually rest on."
defect: The quoted ranges are Jaccard-only, but the verdicts do not rest on Jaccard. Two of the paper's borderline verdicts are produced by containment alone, against a Jaccard reading that is clean. Under containment the same believed-clean data reads up to 0.068 and 0.1375 — not an order of magnitude below the 0.1 cut but at or above it. The closing clause therefore asserts coverage of a metric the paragraph never measures, and the paper's own Discussion two paragraphs later says "the containment index is uniformly the more sensitive of the two metrics at short length".
suggested_fix: Either restrict the sentence to the Jaccard census ("the comparison the Jaccard verdicts rest on") and add the containment readings with their own, weaker floor statement, or report both metrics' clean-data ranges and drop "an order of magnitude".

claim: "We report instead what the statistic itself reads on data believed clean on independent grounds."
defect: The non-circularity of the whole rebuilt specificity argument rests on "independent grounds", and those grounds are established for only one of the two reference sets. For Genomic Benchmarks the coordinate-space screen of §3.10/§4.6 is genuinely independent (causally upstream, non-k-mer). For the fourteen GUE tasks the paper presents no coordinate data and no alignment re-measure; the only evidence they are clean is this estimator plus the exact-duplicate census — and the paper itself argues exact-duplicate absence does not certify near-duplicate absence (§3.4: human_nontata_promoters has 0 exact duplicates yet 0.225 near-duplicates at Jaccard ≥0.9). So the GUE half of the reference set is called clean by the estimator being validated, which is precisely the circularity a referee will allege.
suggested_fix: Say which grounds apply to which half: cite §4.6 for the Genomic Benchmarks five, and for GUE state plainly that no independent evidence of cleanliness is available, so that half bounds the estimator's self-consistency rather than its specificity. Note that the GB half alone already covers the training-set-size point (human_ocr_ensembl trains on ~140,000 sequences, three times the 47,356 quoted).

claim: "15-nearest-neighbour's raw −0.684 and naive Bayes's −0.234 become +0.016 and +0.141".
defect: The corrected GaussianNB gap on human_enhancers_ensembl is +0.129, not +0.141. The same sentence's own paragraph states it correctly twenty words earlier ("naive Bayes (+0.129)") and Table 3 states it correctly. +0.141 is the human_nontata_promoters value, pulled into an ensembl sentence. One quantity, two different numbers, same paragraph.
suggested_fix: Change +0.141 to +0.129 at main.tex:274.

claim: "memorizers average +0.122 against +0.166 for the others, and the largest belongs to the MLP" (§4.5; repeated verbatim at main.tex:248 in §4.4).
defect: +0.166 is the mean over four non-memorizers with the MLP silently dropped, while the same clause names the MLP as the largest member of that very group. Computed the way the matching ensembl figure is computed (all five non-memorizers, main.tex:274 "+0.165 for the remaining five"), the number is +0.179. The two datasets are presented as the same statistic but are averaged over different model sets.
suggested_fix: Change +0.166 to +0.179 at main.tex:248 and :276. The conclusion is unaffected and in fact slightly strengthened (the families are more reversed, not less).

claim: "What the experiment establishes is the positive arm, causally and at ten doses."
defect: The sentence contradicts the two sentences immediately preceding it. Those state that all three negatives are of the no-valid-challenger kind and that the sub-threshold arm is not exercised — i.e. that three of the ten doses establish nothing about the condition. The positive arm is exercised at seven doses. Ending the qualification paragraph by re-asserting "ten" hands back exactly what the paragraph was written to give up, and it is the sentence a skeptical referee will quote.
suggested_fix: "...the positive arm, causally and at the seven doses where the condition had anything to say." Consider also softening "P6 holds on all ten doses" (main.tex:124) and "The condition is right on all ten doses" (main.tex:342) to "seven informative doses and three vacuous ones", since §4.10 already applies exactly that discount to the 24-of-24 cross-suite score.

claim: The T1–T13 table is presented as the reproduction manifest for the Tier-1 deepener modules, and REPRODUCE.md:102-108 walks through the newer ones (T12, T13) individually.
defect: There is no entry for the dose-response experiment — the paper's newest and most load-bearing result (§4.11, prediction P6, Table 4's break-a-clean row). Worse, the committed artifact cannot be produced by any single invocation: the module's default DOSES is six doses, the ten-row CSV is a manual merge of two runs (exp_dose.log 6 rows + exp_dose_fine.log 4 rows), and the module overwrites rather than merges — the exact bug the exp_gue merge block calls out as "the same bug exp_roster.py and exp_tuning.py both had". Any subset re-run silently destroys the committed file; that happened during this audit.
suggested_fix: Add a T14 row with the explicit ten-dose --doses list, and port the exp_gue merge-by-key block into exp_dose_response.py keyed on `condition`.

claim: "The task list is given explicitly because the module's default also censuses the two unregistered mouse tasks, which the committed CSV deliberately excludes."
defect: The committed CSV does not exclude them. results/gue_census.csv contains mouse_0 and mouse_1 as its last two rows. As a consequence the documented T12 command produces a 15-row CSV while the committed artifact has 17 rows, so a reproducer will see a diff and not know which side is wrong. (The merge logic itself is correct — this is a documentation defect, not a data one.)
suggested_fix: Either drop the two mouse rows from the committed CSV, or reword to say they are included but flagged registered=False and excluded from the 3-of-15 tally (which the log already states).

claim: §3.13: "We therefore apply (2) only where the intermediate band is small, and report the band's size wherever we use it."
defect: §4.11 is the paper's heaviest use of eq. (2) — ten applications — and reports the intermediate [0.5,0.9) band size at none of the doses. The self-imposed protocol is stated in Methods and then not followed in the section that most depends on it. The band is in fact small, so the result stands; but a referee checking protocol compliance will find the gap and have no way to know it is harmless.
suggested_fix: Add one clause to §4.11: "the intermediate band is 1.2-1.5% across all ten doses, so the two-stratum approximation holds throughout." Emitting the band fraction as a CSV column would make this checkable.

claim: §3.3 ("Expanded nine-model roster") registers all six pre-committed predictions, introducing "A sixth, P6, was committed in the dose-response module of §4.11" before "A fifth, P5, was committed in the tuning module of §3.9".
defect: Out-of-order enumeration inside one sentence, and two of the six registrations belong to experiments (dose-response, tuning) unrelated to the nine-model roster the subsection is about. P6 in particular is registered by a forward reference into Results, and the dose-response experiment has no Methods subsection of its own — its construction, dose grid, matching procedure and phi* estimator are described only in §4.11.
suggested_fix: Swap the P5 and P6 clauses, and either retitle §3.3 to cover the pre-registration generally or move the P5/P6 registrations into §3.11 and a short new Methods paragraph for the dose grid.

claim: "On human_nontata_promoters the corrected gaps do not separate the families---memorizers average $+0.122$ against $+0.166$ for the others, and the largest belongs to the MLP"
defect: The +0.166 is the mean over only FOUR non-memorizers, computed with the MLP excluded — while the same clause names the MLP as the largest gap. Recomputing from results/graded_gap_corrected.csv, the five human_nontata_promoters non-memorizers are MLP 0.2294, HGB 0.1833, LinearSVC 0.2007, LR 0.1388, GaussianNB 0.1410; their mean is 0.17864 = +0.179. Dropping the MLP gives (0.1833+0.2007+0.1388+0.1410)/4 = 0.16595 = +0.166, i.e. exactly the printed figure. The Round-10 fix (+0.166 -> +0.179, "now includes the MLP") landed at main.tex:248 but NOT at main.tex:276, so the paper now states two different values for the identical quantity in the same section.
