suggested_fix: Either report the 33.3% band in §4.7 and state that the acceptors call is outside the regime §3.9 permits (reducing the admissible informative calls to one, on enhancers, where the band is 0.0%), or drop the acceptors call from the count and rewrite "both pairs where it had anything to say" and "two informative calls" accordingly.

claim: The module registers REPRODUCE.md as a checked document (DOCS["reproduce"]) and its rule 4 states "Check the RESULTS DOCUMENTS too, not just the manuscript. Half the round-11 and round-12 findings were paper/results-document divergence, which a manuscript-only gate cannot see by construction." The round-13 hand-off states the tool "now reads TIER1_FINDINGS.md and REPRODUCE.md as well as paper/main.tex."
defect: No check in the module ever references "reproduce". The registration at line 46 is dead: the file is opened by no predicate, so REPRODUCE.md has exactly zero gate coverage. This is the one file whose round-13 fix (-12.1 → -12.0 pts) is now ungated, and that same number has already regressed twice — audit_findings.csv rows 339 (round 11) and 353/358 (round 12) are all the same REPRODUCE.md:61 figure. The gate advertises coverage of the file with the worst regression history in the project and provides none.
suggested_fix: Add checks that anchor REPRODUCE.md:61 to results/results_table.csv (orig 0.9317, corrected 0.8117, delta 0.1200 → 12.0 pts), and extend --self-test to mutate the "reproduce" and "findings" documents, not only "paper" — as written, every non-manuscript check is exempt from the vacuity proof the module claims as rule 3.

claim: near() docstring: "The value must appear INSIDE the window matched by `context`. This is the rule-1 check… so a correct copy of the number elsewhere in the file cannot rescue a corrupted one here." The module asserts 50/50 checks pass and 5/5 mutations detected.
defect: near() tests only set membership of a token in a ~460-character window, so it is blind to transposition of two values that both live in the same window — the defect class check_intervals_are_labelled was written for after round 12 ("an interval labelled as the cluster bootstrap when it was the combined-source one"). Every paired claim in the gate is exposed. Five novel mutations, none in the --self-test roster, pass 50/50 with zero failures.
suggested_fix: For paired values, assert the ordered rendering (e.g. the literal substring "$+0.292$ against $+0.165$") rather than two independent membership tests; and add checks for the 25.0% NT figure and the discussion-section cohesion restatement, which currently have none.

claim: "On human_enhancers_ensembl at π=0.2, correcting the split lowers AUPRC 0.622→0.477, MCC 0.422→0.182, and minority recall 0.258→0.070, while accuracy barely moves (0.844→0.808); human_nontata_promoters shows the same pattern. Accuracy at threshold 0.5 is thus the wrong metric under imbalance, and the appropriate metrics show the inflation even more starkly."
defect: human_nontata_promoters does not show the same pattern, and the generalization in the following sentence is contradicted by two of the five prevalence-aware metrics the methods section (§3.6, line 149) commits to. On nontata the minority recall — the metric that collapses most dramatically on ensembl (0.258→0.070) — does not fall at all under correction, and balanced accuracy falls by less than plain accuracy at both imbalanced settings, i.e. the opposite of "even more starkly". The ensembl-only numbers are quoted; the discordant second-dataset numbers are in the same committed CSV and are compressed into "the same pattern".
suggested_fix: Replace "shows the same pattern" with the actual split — on human_nontata_promoters MCC (0.785→0.682) and AUPRC (0.949→0.813) reproduce the effect while balanced accuracy and minority recall do not — and restrict the generalization to the threshold-free prevalence-aware metrics rather than "the appropriate metrics".

claim: check_crosssuite_counts registers two anti-regression guards for the results document: says("findings", "of 12 independent", want=False) and says("findings", "twelve are leaky", want=False), labelled "findings no longer says 12 independent" / "…twelve", described in the module header as covering the round-12/13 regression that "lived in the findings document, not the paper".
defect: The second guard cannot match the regression it exists to prevent. The round-13 fix was at results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md:33, where the sentence is line-wrapped as "**Three independent Nucleotide Transformer tasks of eleven are\n   leaky**" — the literal "twelve are leaky" can never appear because "are" and "leaky" are separated by a newline and three spaces. Reverting the exact round-13 fix therefore passes the gate clean. (The first guard, "of 12 independent", does cover the separate numeral form at TIER1_FINDINGS.md:599.)
suggested_fix: Guard on "tasks of twelve" (the wrap-independent prefix) rather than "twelve are leaky", or normalize whitespace in says()/occurs() before matching; and make absent() fail rather than pass when its context regex does not match.

claim: "The intraclass correlation is high ($0.91$--$0.99$) yet the design effect is small ($1.06$--$1.17$)"
defect: The two ranges in the same clause are computed over different sets of rows. The design-effect range 1.06–1.17 spans all four measured rows (1.056, 1.056, 1.145, 1.169), but the ICC range 0.91–0.99 excludes the lowest measured ICC, 0.7794 (human_nontata_promoters LR_k6), which sits in the same table. A reader is told the ICC is uniformly high across the datasets where the design effect was computed; on a quarter of those rows it is 0.78.
suggested_fix: State the ICC range as $0.78$--$0.99$, or scope both ranges to the same rows (e.g. the two random-forest drops, ICC $0.91$--$0.99$, deff $1.06$--$1.17$).

claim: Rule 1: "ANCHOR every check to the passage that makes the claim... the value must appear inside the matched window" — presented as the fix for round 13's whole-document matching, and the basis of ~20 near() checks.
defect: near() decides with a bare substring test, `ok = any(t in window for t in toks)`, with no digit boundary. Any corruption that leaves the expected rendering as a PREFIX of the corrupted one passes. This is not hypothetical precision-fiddling: the paper writes the nonTATA cohesion as $0.08$ at main.tex:392 and $0.083$ at main.tex:368, and the check for 0.08 provably cannot tell them apart.
suggested_fix: In near(), require a boundary after the token, e.g. search `re.escape(t) + r'(?!\d)'` against the window instead of `t in window`.

claim: Rule 2: "ASSERT OCCURRENCE COUNTS where a value should appear a known number of times, so corrupting one of several sites drops the count and fails." The rebuild commit b8fb835 states the old gate's central defect was that "the paper quotes most headline values at three or four sites... so corrupting any single one left the others to satisfy the check."
defect: Rule 2 is implemented in exactly one of the seven check groups (check_manipulation's s.count, :224) plus one occurs() call (:322). Every other multiply-quoted headline value is guarded by a single anchored near(), so corrupting any of its other sites is silent — the identical failure mode the rebuild was for. Most damning: the nonTATA non-memorizer mean is quoted at main.tex:248 AND :276, and round 10 filed it explicitly as "main.tex:276 ... repeated verbatim at main.tex:248" (audit_findings.csv rows for R10/R11, five separate reports of +0.166). The gate anchors :276 and is blind at :248 — it would not have caught the single most-repeated finding of rounds 10-11.
suggested_fix: For each multiply-quoted value, add an occurs() assertion on the exact rendering with the true site count (e.g. "+0.461" 2x, "0.461" 3x, "$3$ of $15$" 2x, "$0.96$" 3x), so any single stale site drops the count.

claim: Docstring rule 4 and the --self-test contract: the gate "reads TIER1_FINDINGS.md and REPRODUCE.md as well as the paper, since half the round-11 and round-12 findings were paper/results divergence", and --self-test "corrupts one site of five multiply-quoted values and REQUIRES the gate to fail on each", failing the run on any check that cannot fail.
defect: self_test() mutates only `_cache["paper"]` (line 391). It never perturbs the findings or reproduce documents, so it provides zero assurance that any non-manuscript check can fail. The half of the defect population rule 4 was written for is exactly the half --self-test cannot police, and a findings-document check that silently regressed to vacuity would still be reported as a passing gate with "5/5 mutations detected".
suggested_fix: Add findings/reproduce mutations to the self_test mutation list (e.g. corrupt TIER1_FINDINGS.md "of eleven" and its GUE-table jac@0.7 minimum) so every document with registered checks is proven to be able to fail.

claim: Module docstring rule 4 ("Check the RESULTS DOCUMENTS too") and commit b8fb835: "it reads TIER1_FINDINGS.md and REPRODUCE.md as well as the paper". REPRODUCE.md:97 in turn advertises the gate (T15) as "exit 1 if a manuscript number disagrees with its source CSV".
defect: REPRODUCE.md is registered in DOCS at line 46 but has ZERO checks. `grep -n '"reproduce"' audit/tools/check_numbers.py` returns only line 46, the registration itself; no near/absent/says/occurs call anywhere in the module passes where="reproduce". The document is opened by nothing and asserted about by nothing. This is precisely the defect class round 13 filed against the previous version — "a docstring claiming coverage it did not have" — reintroduced in the rebuild. Concretely it leaves this round's own REPRODUCE.md:61 fix (-12.1 -> -12.0 pts, the file's self-described "quickest check") ungated, and that figure has now been filed as a finding in three separate rounds (audit_findings.csv rows for R11, R12 x2, R13).
suggested_fix: Register the headline reproduction: near("reproduce", r"reproduces the canonical result", 0.9317) / 0.8117 / 12.0 recomputed from results/results_table.csv, and assert REPRODUCE.md agrees with results/results.md rather than with the frozen 3-seed summary_final.csv.

claim: self_test docstring: "Each mutation corrupts ONE site of a value the manuscript states at several. Under the old whole-document matcher every one of these passed."
defect: False for at least three of the five mutations, and misleading for a fourth. The claim is what makes 5/5 read as evidence against the round-13 failure mode, but four of the five mutations corrupt the very site the check anchors to — the easy case — and two of those target values with only one site in the manuscript, where a whole-document matcher would also have failed. Only mutation 3 (the break-a-clean interval, an occurs-count check) genuinely exercises multi-site coverage. The suite therefore over-reports the assurance it provides.
suggested_fix: Either retarget mutations 1, 2, 4 and 5 at the non-anchored sites (main.tex:248, :258, :335, :368), which currently pass, or restate the docstring to claim only what the suite tests.

claim: §4.9: "Counting independent tasks, three of eleven in the original release are leaky and three more borderline" — i.e. five of the eleven independent Nucleotide Transformer tasks are clean. The count reaches the Abstract ("Three of eleven independent Nucleotide Transformer tasks are similarly leaky") and the Conclusion (main.tex:409). audit/tools/check_numbers.py:302-324 pins it as "3+3+5 = 11".
defect: The NT census was run with training sets capped at 20,000 rows on 8 of the 13 shipped tasks, including 4 of the 5 tasks declared clean and all 3 declared borderline. Re-running the repo's own module at full scale (`exp_crosssuite_census --cap 100000`) flips three of the five clean verdicts to borderline. This is precisely the failure the paper's own Conclusion (main.tex:411) makes practice recommendation #1 against — "Audit at full dataset scale, since subsampling can make a heavily leaky dataset look clean" — and which main.tex:392 says the authors "paid that cost ourselves on the GUE census ... which we therefore re-ran in full". The NT census, the one whose count reaches the Abstract, was never re-run. The paper's only caveat (main.tex:167) is that "every reported fraction is a lower bound", which does not tell the reader that verdicts flip; the module's own docstring (audit/experiments/exp_crosssuite_census.py:41-42) is explicit that "'clean at the cap' is provisional and is reported as such", and it is not reported as such anywhere in the manuscript. The paper already documented this exact flip once, on GUE's emp_H3K4me3 (main.tex:335, capped containment 0.093 → 0.137 at full scale) — the same histone mark whose NT counterpart flips here.
suggested_fix: Re-run the NT-original census at full scale for all 13 tasks and restate §4.9, the Abstract and the Conclusion with the resulting counts (on the four tasks I re-ran: three leaky, six borderline, two clean). If a full re-run is not done, the counts must be labelled verdict-level lower bounds and the capped tasks named, and main.tex:392's "we paid that cost ourselves" must be scoped to GUE. Add a check_numbers assertion that crosssuite_census.csv has subsampled==False on every row, mirroring the existing GUE `train_frac_used.eq(1.0).all()` check that would have caught this.

claim: §4.10: "Resampling whole within-test near-duplicate components as blocks ... widens the CIs by $1.0$--$1.8\times$ but flips no significance verdict: the random-forest drop still excludes zero on both datasets (\textit{human\_enhancers\_ensembl} $[0.156,0.172]$; \textit{human\_nontata\_promoters} $[0.092,0.126]$)".
defect: The ensembl interval is from a superseded 1,000-replicate run and disagrees with the file that supplies every other quantity in the same sentence. results/cluster_bootstrap_full.csv (10,000 replicates) — the sole source for the nontata interval, the ICC, the design effect, the CRVE cross-check and both combined-source intervals quoted alongside it — gives [0.1552, 0.1727], i.e. [0.155, 0.173]. results/bh_correction_frozen.csv, the frozen multiplicity artifact, consumes [0.1552, 0.1727] too, so the manuscript disagrees with its own BH input. The stated widening range is drawn from the same superseded run: recomputed from cluster_bootstrap_full.csv the four sample-vs-cluster width ratios are 1.35, 1.79, 1.22 and 1.53, so the range is 1.2–1.8×, not 1.0–1.8×. This is round-13 finding results/audit_findings.csv row 381 (status "confirmed"), whose suggested fix — quote both intervals from cluster_bootstrap_full.csv and pin them in check_numbers — was not applied in either part.
suggested_fix: Change main.tex:359 to $[0.155,0.173]$ and $1.2$--$1.8\times$, and add a check_numbers check pinning both leaky cluster intervals and the widening range to results/cluster_bootstrap_full.csv.

claim: §4.8: "Nineteen of the $20$ cells drop with cluster-bootstrap CIs excluding zero ... the sole exception is one \textit{human\_nontata\_promoters} cell (dropout $0.6$, weight decay $10^{-4}$) where heavy dropout under-fits, leaving no inflation to lose (accuracy rises $0.020$ after correction)."
defect: "Leaving no inflation to lose" reads as a null result, and the sentence's framing (an exception to "CIs excluding zero") tells the reader the interval covers zero. It does not: that cell's cluster-bootstrap CI is [-0.0349, -0.0044], which excludes zero on the negative side. All 20 of 20 cells have drop_excl0_cluster=True in the committed CSV. The cell is not a null, it is a statistically supported reversal — the corrected split is significantly better there — and that is a materially different fact about the only counter-evidence cell in the deep-model section, which the paper leans on to show it is not cherry-picking the grid.
suggested_fix: Rephrase to "the sole cell that does not drop is ... where accuracy instead rises 0.020, with a cluster-bootstrap CI [-0.035,-0.004] that excludes zero — heavy dropout under-fits the as-shipped split, so there is no inflation to lose and the corrected split is genuinely easier for it."

claim: "Headline reproduction (quickest check): `python -m audit.pipeline.run_audit` reproduces the canonical result: human_nontata_promoters, **RF k6**: original **0.9317** -> homology-aware **0.8117** (**-12.0 pts**)".
defect: The arithmetic fix applied since round 13 is correct (0.9317-0.8117 = 0.1200), but the number is still labelled "the canonical result" while being computed under the superseded `predict_proba>=0.5` decision rule that the manuscript's own canonical NOTE (main.tex:37-46) exists to retire. Under the canonical convention the same quantity is 0.9284 -> 0.8101 = 11.8 pts (five-seed mean), or 10.8 pts on the seed-0 partition. results/reconciled_numbers.md:64-65 documents that the baseline itself moves with the rule (0.9317 under `>=0.5` vs 0.9284 under `.predict()`). A reproducer following the Data Availability link runs the documented quickest check, gets 12.0, and has no pointer explaining why the paper's headline is 11.8. Round-12 finding results/audit_findings.csv row 358 recommended both the number fix and "add one clause noting that run_audit uses the legacy predict_proba>=0.5 rule, so this number is not the paper's canonical 11.8-pt headline"; only the number was changed.
suggested_fix: Replace "the canonical result" with "the legacy `predict_proba>=0.5` path" and append: "this is not the paper's canonical headline (11.8 pts, 0.9284 -> 0.8101, `.predict()` + five-seed mean); see results/reconciled_numbers.md §5."

claim: Module docstring: checks "ANCHOR every check to the passage that makes the claim", "NEVER write a predicate that cannot fail", "Check the RESULTS DOCUMENTS too"; `--self-test` reports 5/5 mutations detected and 50/50 checks pass.
defect: The rebuilt gate is far stronger than its predecessor but three classes of vacuity survive, and they are what let the other findings in this round persist. (1) Pair-swap blindness: where two related values live in one 420-character window, the two checks are interchangeable and swapping the values passes. This affects 8 of the 50 checks. (2) REPRODUCE.md is registered in DOCS (line 46) and named in docstring rule 4, but no check references it — corrupting its headline number is undetected, which is the same "docstring claiming coverage it does not have" defect round 13 found in v1. (3) `absent()` returns PASS when its context regex fails to match (line 121, "context absent, so the regression cannot be present"), so anchor drift silently disarms it. Separately, `self_test()` mutates only the `paper` document, so no findings/reproduce check is mutation-tested, and the registered surface excludes the headline drops (11.8/16.5), Table 2, Table 3 and the coordinate counts — corrupting any of those passes.
suggested_fix: For paired values, assert ordered adjacency (e.g. the literal "average $+0.292$ against $+0.165$") rather than two independent membership tests on one window. Add at least one check per registered document — starting with the REPRODUCE.md headline pair — or drop "reproduce" from DOCS and from the docstring. Make `absent()` return False when its context is not found, or pair every context-scoped `absent` with an existence assertion on the same anchor. Extend `self_test()` to mutate `findings` and `reproduce` too. Register the headline drops, Table 2 and Table 3 against their CSVs.

claim: Referee verdict and the single biggest remaining weakness.
defect: Verdict: MAJOR REVISION, on the strength of the blocker alone — a count stated in the Abstract and Conclusion is falsified by the paper's own protocol at the scale its own Conclusion mandates, and the fix requires re-running the NT census, not re-wording. Everything else I checked recomputes exactly: Tables 1-4, the nine-model roster, all corrected and raw graded gaps, the dose-response, the chromosome and alignment controls, the regularization path, the tuning result, the imbalance panel, the injected multiclass, the coordinate counts (77,421 = 2x36,487 + 4,447 on 40,934 distinct), the label concordance, BH, cohesion, canonical k-mers, GC-matching and the CNN grid all match their CSVs to the last quoted digit. Biggest remaining weakness (substantive, not a defect): the headline contribution is still n=1. Claim II rests on one dataset; the second leaky dataset is honestly conceded partial on five independent signals; the nine-model roster, the manipulations and the dose-response all strengthen the mechanism on that same one dataset; and the only external suite tested produces a null. The paper is unusually scrupulous about this — it says so in the Abstract, twice in the Introduction, in §4.3, §4.5 and the Conclusion — but a Bioinformatics Advances referee will still ask whether an existence proof on one dataset, plus a diagnostic condition with two informative out-of-sample calls, supports a title that generalizes. The most valuable single addition would be a third leaky dataset from outside these two suites where the reordering reproduces prospectively from the as-shipped φ* screen; short of that, softening "a genomic benchmark suite" toward the demonstrated scope in the title would preempt the objection.
suggested_fix: No change required for the nit itself. Address the blocker, apply the three minors, and the manuscript is otherwise submission-ready.

claim: §4.10: "Condition (2) gets its first out-of-sample test here, and on both pairs where it had anything to say it was right. It predicted no swap for splice_sites_acceptors RF-versus-HGB ($\varphi=0.077$ against $\varphi^{*}=0.257$)..." and, at line 328, "there the condition correctly identified a possible inversion and correctly predicted it would not occur". These are the "two informative calls, both correct" on which "now externally stress-tested rather than merely asserted" rests.
defect: The paper applies eq. (2) to a task its own Methods rules out of scope, and omits the disclosure the same Methods sentence promises. main.tex:175 states: "That band is negligible on human_enhancers_ensembl (1.4%...) but not elsewhere---22.4% on human_nontata_promoters (error up to 0.031) and about a third on the Nucleotide Transformer splice tasks, WHERE THE APPROXIMATION ERROR EXCEEDS THE MARGINS IT WOULD BE USED TO ADJUDICATE. We therefore apply (2) only where the intermediate band is small, and report the band's size wherever we use it." splice_sites_acceptors is exactly such a task. Both halves of the commitment are broken: eq. (2) is applied in the excluded regime, and no band size appears at either point of use — the word "band" occurs at only two lines in the whole manuscript, 175 (the Methods commitment) and 342 (the dose-response, which does honour it: "As §m-law requires wherever (2) is applied, we report the intermediate [0.5,0.9) band"). The exclusion is not among the "Three limits keep this modest" listed in the same paragraph, so it is not disclosed alongside the claim. Recorded as a blocker in round 13 (results/audit_findings.csv row 377, status=confirmed) and not fixed since.
suggested_fix: Either (a) drop the splice_sites_acceptors call from the out-of-sample evidence, restate line 326 as ONE informative call, and move the pair to a disclosed "excluded by the band criterion" note; or (b) keep it and report the 33.3% band at both points of use, stating that the reconstruction error on that band dwarfs the 0.0032 margin so the call carries no evidential weight. Line 328 needs the same treatment. Then add a check_numbers check asserting that every task on which phi* is quoted in main.tex has a reported mid-band below the Methods threshold.

claim: Under "Headline reproduction (quickest check)": "`python -m audit.pipeline.run_audit` reproduces the canonical result: human_nontata_promoters, **RF k6**: original **0.9317** -> homology-aware **0.8117** (**-12.0 pts**)", followed by "`audit/pipeline/run_robustness_full.py` independently re-loads and re-fits the full dataset from scratch and reproduces the same nontata full-scale numbers, so the headline is reproduced by two independent paths."
defect: This round's edit fixed the round-12 arithmetic minor (0.932/0.811/-12.1 → 0.9317/0.8117/-12.0) but left the round-13 MAJOR untouched (results/audit_findings.csv, file=REPRODUCE.md:61, round=13, severity=major, status=confirmed). Two defects persist. (1) The number offered as "the canonical result" is not the paper's canonical result and is computed under a decision rule the paper explicitly declares it does not use: main.tex:37-46 fixes ONE convention everywhere (.predict()/argmax + 5-seed mean), giving 0.9284 → 0.8101 = 11.8 pts — the abstract's number. 0.9317/0.8117 is the retired predict_proba>=0.5 / 3-seed convention. Neither of round 13's two suggested remedies was applied. (2) The "two independent paths ... same numbers" claim is false against the committed CSVs: the second path gives 0.8105 (12.1 pts), not 0.8117 (12.0 pts). A reviewer running the documented quickest check cannot obtain 11.8 by either path.
suggested_fix: Apply the recorded one-line fix at run_audit.py:157 and update the block to 0.9284 -> 0.8101 (-11.8 pts); or relabel the block explicitly as the legacy predict_proba/3-seed convention, delete the word "canonical", point readers at step2_rf_seeds/step_variance_ci for the headline, and replace "the same nontata full-scale numbers" with the two actual values (0.8117 vs 0.8105) and why they differ.

claim: Module docstring rule 4: "Check the RESULTS DOCUMENTS too, not just the manuscript. Half the round-11 and round-12 findings were paper/results-document divergence, which a manuscript-only gate cannot see by construction." REPRODUCE.md is registered at line 46 as one of the three DOCS, and the round-13 remit records the rebuilt gate as "it now reads TIER1_FINDINGS.md and REPRODUCE.md as well as paper/main.tex".
defect: REPRODUCE.md is registered but never read by any check. No check function calls doc("reproduce"), near("reproduce", ...), says("reproduce", ...), occurs("reproduce", ...) or absent("reproduce", ...). The file is loaded into DOCS and then ignored, so the gate reports 50/50 PASS on a document it does not inspect. This is the same class of defect round 13 caught and rule 4 was written to prevent — a docstring claiming coverage the module does not have. Critically, --self-test cannot surface it: self_test() only ever assigns _cache["paper"], so no mutation of REPRODUCE.md (or of TIER1_FINDINGS.md) is ever attempted, and a document with zero checks is indistinguishable from one whose checks all pass.
suggested_fix: Add checks that anchor REPRODUCE.md's headline block to results/step2_seed_variance.csv (or drop REPRODUCE.md from DOCS and delete the coverage claim from the docstring). Extend self_test() to mutate each registered document, and make it fail if any document in DOCS has zero checks referencing it — a document with no checks should be reported as unmonitored, not silently pass.

claim: Docstring rule 1: "ANCHOR every check to the passage that makes the claim, never to the document"; rule 2: "ASSERT OCCURRENCE COUNTS where a value should appear a known number of times, so corrupting one of several sites drops the count and fails." The gate reports 50/50 checks pass and 5/5 mutations detected.
defect: The anchoring machinery works, but its coverage misses the manuscript's four tables, both abstract headline numbers, and the Results-section statement of the cohesion result. Two anchors are mis-targeted specifically: (a) check_corrected_gaps anchors 1-NN's corrected gap 0.461 to the §4.5 prose (context "definitional memorizer", main.tex:274) with no occurrence count, but 0.461 appears at TWO sites — the second is the Gap_bal cell of Table 3 (main.tex:258), the paper's headline roster table, which is therefore unchecked; (b) check_cohesion's context regex `cohesion \$0\.\d\d\$ and` matches only main.tex:392 (the Discussion restatement), never main.tex:368 where the cohesion result is actually reported in Results, so the Results statement is unanchored. Mutation testing with 13 defects the gate has not been shown: 12 pass undetected. Answering the round-14 question directly — no, the gate would not catch every defect rounds 10-13 found: round 13's own recorded fix for the ensembl cluster-bootstrap interval ("Add a check_numbers check pinning both cluster intervals to cluster_bootstrap_full.csv, which would have caught this") was not implemented.
suggested_fix: Add occurs()-style multi-site assertions for every value stated in both a table and its prose (start with Table 3's Gap_bal/Gap_raw columns against results/graded_gap_corrected.csv, Table 2's leak fractions against results/exp_gb1_containment.csv, and the abstract's 11.8/16.5 against results/step2_seed_variance.csv). Re-anchor check_cohesion to main.tex:368 with an occurrence count of 2 so both the Results and Discussion sites are pinned. Add the round-13 cluster-interval check. Replace places=0 integer tokens with a surrounding-context string (e.g. "score $3$ of $15$") so the predicate cannot be satisfied by an incidental digit.

claim: §4.11: "the random-forest drop still excludes zero on both datasets (human_enhancers_ensembl $[0.156,0.172]$; human_nontata_promoters $[0.092,0.126]$)", presented as one cluster-bootstrap procedure applied to two datasets.
defect: The ensembl interval matches neither the cluster bootstrap nor the sample bootstrap in the CSV the same sentence's ICC, design effect, CRVE cross-check and combined-source intervals all come from. Both endpoints are rounded inward by one unit in the last place, narrowing the reported interval. The nontata interval in the same parenthesis is exact, so the two are not from the same run. Recorded as a round-13 minor (results/audit_findings.csv row 381, status=confirmed) and not fixed.
suggested_fix: Quote [0.155,0.173] and [0.092,0.126], both from results/cluster_bootstrap_full.csv, and recompute the "widens the CIs by 1.0--1.8x" range from that file alone (the four rows give 1.22-1.79x).

claim: Methods §3.13: "That band is negligible on human_enhancers_ensembl ($1.4\%$ of the test set, reconstruction error $0.002$) but not elsewhere---$22.4\%$ on human_nontata_promoters (error up to $0.031$)..."
defect: The 0.031 reconstruction error is not produced by any committed CSV. The parallel ensembl figure (0.002) is the maximum absolute two-bin reconstruction error in results/inversion_law_anchors.csv (0.0023), so that is the statistic the sentence is quoting; the same statistic for human_nontata_promoters is 0.0219, i.e. 0.022. No other candidate matches either. The error is overstated rather than understated, so it does not inflate a claim — but it is a stated number with no source, in the passage that defines the scope rule the blocker above turns on.
suggested_fix: Replace "error up to $0.031$" with "error up to $0.022$", or name the file and column the 0.031 comes from and use the same source for the ensembl figure.

claim: Methods §"Cross-suite census and re-ranking" states: "Training sets are capped at $20{,}000$ sequences for the census; capping can only remove potential near-duplicate partners, so every reported fraction is a lower bound."
defect: This is the pre-Round-14 protocol and it is no longer true. The census was re-run uncapped, and the manuscript's own Results section says so explicitly at main.tex:322 — "We report this at full scale: an earlier pass capped training sets at 20,000 and returned three borderline and five clean, and re-running uncapped moved three histone tasks across the cut." Methods and Results now assert opposite protocols for the same numbers, and Methods asserts a lower-bound status that the shipped data contradicts. A reader who takes Methods at face value will read the six borderline and two clean NT verdicts as provisional-at-cap rather than as full-scale measurements — which inverts the paper's own point that capped clean verdicts are the failure mode its first practice recommendation warns against.
suggested_fix: Replace the sentence at main.tex:167 with the full-scale protocol, e.g. "The census is run at full scale: no training set is subsampled, so no reported fraction is capped-lower-bounded (the length-dependent lower bound of §Limitations still applies)." Optionally note the superseded capped pass here with a forward reference to §4.9 rather than restating the cap as current method.

claim: Tier-1 table row T4 documents the reproduction command for the cross-suite census as `python -m audit.experiments.exp_crosssuite_census`, with stated output `crosssuite_census.csv`.
defect: The documented command does not regenerate the committed artifact — it silently overwrites it with the stale, capped numbers that were the Round-14 blocker. `exp_crosssuite_census.py` defaults `--cap` to 20000, and eight of thirteen NT-original tasks exceed that, so the documented invocation stratify-subsamples them and, via the merge-by-(suite,task) path, replaces the committed full-scale rows in place. That flips the three histone containment values back below the cut (H3K4me1 0.135→~0.094, H3K4me3 0.154→~0.088, H3K36me3 0.143→~0.087), turning the paper's "three of eleven leaky and six more borderline, leaving only two clean" into the superseded 3/3/5 tally and breaking check_numbers. The GUE census got exactly this treatment right — T12 is documented as `--cap 100000` with a bolded "**T12 must be run uncapped**" note — so the omission is specific to T4, the module that produced the Round-14 blocker.
suggested_fix: Change the T4 command to `python -m audit.experiments.exp_crosssuite_census --cap 100000` (max n_train is 53,276, so nothing is truncated) and add the same uncapped note T12 carries. Better: flip the module default to no cap (or make `--cap` required), so the bare documented command cannot regenerate lower-bound rows over a full-scale artifact.

claim: Methods §3.13 (Cross-suite census and re-ranking) states: "Training sets are capped at $20{,}000$ sequences for the census; capping can only remove potential near-duplicate partners, so every reported fraction is a lower bound."
defect: This is stale and now false. The census that produces the paper's headline cross-suite count was re-run uncapped, and Results §4.10 (line 322) says so explicitly and treats the capped pass as the error it corrected: "We report this at full scale: an earlier pass capped training sets at $20{,}000$ and returned three borderline and five clean, and re-running uncapped moved three histone tasks across the cut." The Methods section therefore describes a protocol the paper elsewhere identifies as wrong, and describes it as the one used. It also contradicts the paper's own first practice recommendation ("Audit at full dataset scale", line 411) and the Discussion's account of paying that cost (line 392). A reader taking Methods at face value will believe the 3-leaky/6-borderline/2-clean tally is a subsampled lower bound produced by the very defect §4.10 says was removed.
suggested_fix: Replace the sentence at line 167 with the actual protocol, e.g. "The census is run at full scale with no training-set cap (results/crosssuite_census.csv records n_train_used = n_train_full for every task); an earlier capped pass is reported in \S\ref{sec:r-census} as a corrected error." Every reported fraction remains a lower bound for the length-cap reason of \S\ref{sec:m-measure}, so that clause can be retained on its correct justification rather than on subsampling.

claim: In the estimator-specificity defence (Discussion, "What the detector detects, and one false positive"): "The second is provenance: four of the five clean Genomic Benchmarks datasets have a documented merge-and-deduplicate step and the fifth, \textit{demo\_human\_or\_worm}, is a cross-species disjoint draw; none has rows on duplicated coordinates. ... the statistic reads $0.001$ to $0.016$ across them."
defect: Two independent off-by-one errors in the passage that carries the paper's answer to the most obvious reviewer attack (are your leak fractions false positives?). (a) There are four clean Genomic Benchmarks datasets, not five — the paper reclassifies demo_coding_vs_intergenomic_seqs as borderline in the abstract (line 49), §4.1 (line 185), Table 2 (line 198), §4.13 (line 364) and the Conclusion (line 407), and 'four clean' appears at all five of those sites. (b) Of the four clean datasets only three have a documented merge-and-deduplicate step; two of the five non-leaky datasets, not one, are disjoint draws. The quoted range 0.001–0.016 spans exactly the four clean datasets and silently excludes demo_coding, whose Jaccard reading is 0.078 — close enough to the 0.1 verdict cut that including it would break the sentence's own conclusion two lines later that "the floor of this estimator ... is an order of magnitude below the verdict cut". A reader reconstructing the evidence base gets a set of five whose stated statistic range is wrong, and a provenance breakdown that does not match the paper's own construction table.
suggested_fix: Rewrite as: "four of the five clean" -> "three of the four clean"; "and the fifth, demo_human_or_worm" -> "and the fourth, demo_human_or_worm". The quoted range 0.001–0.016 and the conclusion then stand unchanged. If demo_coding is to be kept in the argument at all, it must be named separately as the borderline dataset reading 0.078, with the order-of-magnitude claim restated accordingly.

claim: §4.2: "All five non-leaky deltas include zero for the memorizing random forest as well as the linear models (the largest, \textit{drosophila\_enhancers\_stark} RF, is $+0.024$ with 95\% CI $[-0.008,0.058]$)".
defect: The point estimate is right but the interval does not match either recomputed source. Both frozen result files give the cluster-bootstrap interval as [-0.0067, 0.0539]; the paper reports [-0.008, 0.058], which is wider at both ends by more than rounding permits (-0.0067 rounds to -0.007, 0.0539 to 0.054). No file in results/ contains the stated bounds. The error is in the conservative direction and the verdict (interval includes zero, positive control holds) is unaffected, so this is a traceability defect rather than a claim failure — but it is the only clean-dataset interval quoted numerically in the paper and it cannot be reproduced from the release.
suggested_fix: Change $[-0.008,0.058]$ to $[-0.007,0.054]$ to match results/cluster_bootstrap_full.csv, and register the value in the numbers checker so it is pinned to that row.

claim: Methods §3.12 (PDF p.6): "Training sets are capped at $20{,}000$ sequences for the census; capping can only remove potential near-duplicate partners, so every reported fraction is a lower bound." This is the stated protocol for the Nucleotide Transformer cross-suite census that produces the abstract's headline "Three of eleven independent Nucleotide Transformer tasks are similarly leaky and six more borderline."
defect: The Methods description of the census protocol is stale and now directly contradicts both the Results and the committed data. Results §4.10 (main.tex:322) says the opposite in terms: "We report this at full scale: an earlier pass capped training sets at 20,000 and returned three borderline and five clean, and re-running uncapped moved three histone tasks across the cut." Table 2's caption likewise asserts "All leak fractions are full-scale." The R14 fix re-ran the census uncapped but left the Methods paragraph describing the abandoned capped protocol. The contradiction is self-inflicted damage: the paper's own first practice recommendation is "Audit at full dataset scale, since subsampling can make a heavily leaky dataset look clean" (main.tex:411), so a referee reading Methods is told the cross-suite headline was produced by exactly the procedure the paper condemns, and would reasonably discount the 3/6/2 tally. The trailing clause is also now false in the other direction — the fractions are no longer lower bounds from capping, and the code agrees (verdict_is_lower_bound=False on every row).
suggested_fix: Replace the sentence at main.tex:167 with the current protocol, e.g. "The census is run at full scale, with no cap on training-set size; an earlier capped pass is reported in §4.10 together with the verdicts it changed." Delete the now-inapplicable "so every reported fraction is a lower bound" clause, or re-attach it to the length-cap argument in §3.4 where it is still true.

claim: Discussion §5 (PDF p.16): "We paid that cost ourselves on the GUE census, whose first pass capped training sets at $20{,}000$ rows and which we therefore re-ran in full; the leak fractions roughly tripled and one verdict changed, though the conclusion did not." This is the quantitative evidence offered for the paper's first practice recommendation ("Audit at full dataset scale", main.tex:411).
defect: "Roughly tripled" is not supported by the paper's own capped and full-scale GUE runs; it overstates the effect by roughly a factor of two to three. Recomputing every task's capped-to-full ratio from the two logs and the committed census gives a median ratio of 1.15x (Jaccard) and 1.14x (containment), with a maximum anywhere of 2.77x. Seven of the fifteen registered tasks were never capped at all (n_train < 20,000), so their fractions are numerically identical before and after. No task tripled. The claim matters because it is the only quantified instance the Discussion gives of the scale hazard, and a referee spot-checking it against the released logs finds the headline multiplier wrong.
suggested_fix: State the measured magnitude, e.g. "the leak fractions rose by up to 2.8x on the tasks large enough to have been capped (median 1.2x across the suite) and one verdict changed." Alternatively cite the NT census instead, where the re-run moved three verdicts and changed the reported tally from 3/3/5 to 3/6/2 — a materially stronger and correctly stated instance of the same point.

claim: Referee verdict and single biggest remaining weakness. Verdict: MINOR REVISION. The manuscript is careful, unusually well-controlled, and honest about its own failures — the failed P1/P2/P5 pre-registrations, the falsified GUE prediction, the non-monotone CNN grid, the virus_covid false positive, and the vacuousness of the 24/24 condition score are all reported against interest. Every quantitative claim I recomputed from the CSVs matched. The two findings above are prose defects, not evidential ones.
defect: The single biggest remaining weakness is a joint implication the paper never confronts in one place, though each half is disclosed separately. The dataset carrying the flagship reordering claim, human_enhancers_ensembl, is 38.0% byte-identical training copies (§3.4) arising from literal row duplication (§4.6) — so the clean n=1 existence proof is a demonstration about duplicated rows, arguably arithmetic rather than homology. The one dataset in the suite with genuine mutated near-duplicates and zero exact duplicates, human_nontata_promoters, is precisely where the claim degrades to "cautionary partial case" and where the prevalence-corrected graded gap fails to separate model families at all (§4.5). Stated together: the paper's cleanest evidence comes from its least biologically interesting failure mode, and its most homology-like dataset is where the mechanism is not supported. This is a scope limitation rather than an error — the construct-and-break manipulation and the dose-response do carry causal weight — but a reader has to assemble it from §3.4, §4.5 and §4.7 rather than being told it.
suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Discussion scope paragraph (near main.tex:392, where cohesion 0.96 vs 0.08 is already contrasted) acknowledging that the clean demonstration rests on literal duplication while the mutated-near-duplicate case is the partial one, and that separating "duplicated rows reorder rankings" from "homology reorders rankings" needs a dataset with high mutated-near-duplicate content and cohesive clusters — which this suite does not supply. That converts the strongest available reviewer objection into a stated boundary of the claim.

claim: Methods §3.x: "Training sets are capped at $20{,}000$ sequences for the census; capping can only remove potential near-duplicate partners, so every reported fraction is a lower bound."
defect: This describes a protocol that was superseded by the round-14 re-run and is now false. The Methods section flatly contradicts the Results section of the same paper, which states at :322 "We report this at full scale: an earlier pass capped training sets at $20{,}000$ and returned three borderline and five clean, and re-running uncapped moved three histone tasks across the cut." A reader who takes Methods at face value will read all thirteen NT-original leak fractions as lower bounds rather than measurements, and will not understand that the six borderline verdicts are full-scale results. The paper's own §322 calls capping "exactly the failure our own first practice recommendation warns against" — so Methods currently advertises the paper committing the error its Results section takes credit for correcting.
suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with the full-scale statement, e.g. "The census is run at full scale: no training set is subsampled, so no reported fraction is a capping-induced lower bound." (The length-dependent lower-bound caveat at :395 is separate and should stay.)

claim: Contributions list: "a cross-suite check on the Nucleotide Transformer downstream tasks, where three of eleven independent tasks are leaky---one by the same duplicated-coordinate defect, two by cross-species splice-site homology". Repeated verbatim in the Conclusion at main.tex:409.
defect: The attribution of the NT `enhancers` leakage to "the same duplicated-coordinate defect" is unsupported and unverifiable from the data: the NT-original enhancers release ships no coordinate information at all. What was actually measured is byte-identical sequence duplication, which is the downstream signature, not the upstream coordinate cause the phrase asserts. This matters because the coordinate-level defect (77,421 intervals on 40,934 distinct coordinates) is the paper's central causal mechanism, established on human_enhancers_ensembl and manipulated in the break-a-clean/fix-a-leaky experiment; claiming the same coordinate defect recurs in a second, independently built suite reads as external replication of that mechanism when no coordinate evidence exists there. The paper states it correctly in the Results (:322, "25.0% test-to-train leakage that is byte-identical") and so does the results document — only the two most-read passages overstate it.
suggested_fix: In both places replace "the same duplicated-coordinate defect" with what was measured, e.g. "one by outright byte-identical duplication (the signature the coordinate defect produces, though that release ships no coordinates to confirm it)", or simply "one by byte-identical duplication".

claim: §4.2: "The informative consequence is that `human_nontata_promoters`' leak fraction of 0.406 is not a property of the promoter task — NT's equivalent is clean at 0.0059 — but of Genomic Benchmarks' construction of it. That separates task effect from curation effect and corroborates §2."
defect: The number 0.0059 is not supported by any source and does not correspond to either candidate NT promoter task. This is the single load-bearing quantity in the sentence that performs the separation of task effect from curation effect — the argument the reclassification puts most pressure on — and it appears to be a stray value borrowed from an unrelated human_ocr_ensembl delta. The qualitative conclusion survives (both real values are far below the 0.1 cut), but the quoted figure is wrong and a reader checking it against the cited CSV will not find it.
suggested_fix: Replace "clean at 0.0059" with the sourced value and metric, e.g. "clean at 0.0125 under the k-mer Jaccard and 0.0157 under containment (crosssuite_census.csv, NT-original promoter_no_tata)".

claim: §4.1 per-task mechanism table: "| splice_sites_all *(borderline)* | 0.0797 | 0.1067 | 0.0593 | mixed |" — columns are jac@0.7, containment@0.7, exact.
defect: All three values are stale capped-run numbers, retained after the round-14 full-scale re-run updated the CSV this table cites. The table's own header (line 376) names `crosssuite_census.csv` as its source, and every other row in it matches the current CSV — only splice_sites_all was left behind. The containment value is the one that carries the borderline verdict, and the stale 0.1067 sits so close to the 0.1 cut that a reader assessing verdict robustness would draw the opposite conclusion about margin from the true 0.1327.
suggested_fix: Update the row to 0.0977 / 0.1327 / 0.0737. Worth extending check_numbers to assert the §4.1 per-task table against crosssuite_census.csv row-by-row, since this is the one table it does not cover.

claim: Header to the cross-suite census table: "`crosssuite_census.csv`, `crosssuite_exact_verification.csv`. Train sets capped at 20,000; capping only removes near-duplicate partners, so every figure is a lower bound." Followed at :380 by "| NT-original | 13 (11) | **4 (3)** | 6 | 2 |".
defect: Two small consistency problems in the same block. (a) The cap/lower-bound sentence is stale for the same reason as main.tex:167 — it labels the full-scale table beneath it as a set of lower bounds. Unlike the paper, this document contains no later correction adjacent to the table, so a reader of §4 alone is left with the wrong reading; the correction appears only 220 lines later at :598. (b) The NT-original row does not sum: the label says 13 tasks with 11 independent, and the LEAKY column gives both counts as "4 (3)", but the borderline and clean columns give only the independent values (6, 2), so the row reads as 4+6+2=12 of 13. At 13-task level the clean count is 3 (promoter_no_tata, promoter_tata, promoter_all). The NT-revised row below uses the opposite convention, reporting clean=13 rather than 11.
suggested_fix: Replace the cap sentence with the full-scale statement, and make the row's convention uniform, e.g. "| NT-original | 13 (11) | 4 (3) | 6 (6) | 3 (2) |" and "| NT-revised | 13 (11) | 0 | 0 | 13 (11) |".

claim: The cross-suite census table in §4 is captioned as capped and lower-bounded: "`crosssuite_census.csv`, `crosssuite_exact_verification.csv`. Train sets capped at 20,000; capping only removes near-duplicate partners, so every figure is a lower bound."
defect: This is the exact old form of the round-15 blocker, surviving in a live document. It was removed from Methods (paper/main.tex:167 now reads "The census is run at full scale: no training set is subsampled") but not from the companion findings record, where it directly labels the summary table of the re-run full-scale verdicts.
suggested_fix: Replace the caption with the full-scale statement, e.g. "Train sets are not subsampled; every task is censused at its full shipped size (crosssuite_census.csv records n_train_used = n_train_full on every row). An earlier pass capped train at 20,000 and moved three histone verdicts; see §4.2." Extend audit/tools/check_numbers.py to assert the absence of "capped at 20,000" in TIER1_FINDINGS.md's §4 census passage.

claim: The round-8 GUE full-scale blockquote states "The leak fractions rose roughly threefold (`prom_core_all` 0.0054 -> 0.0149) exactly as C1 predicts".
defect: "Roughly threefold" is the characterization round 15 corrected as wrong. It generalizes the single largest movement (itself 2.8x, not 3x) to the whole set, when the median task barely moved and seven of fifteen did not move at all because they were never capped. main.tex:392 was fixed to "rose by up to 2.8x on the tasks large enough to have been capped---the seven below the cap are of course unchanged"; this counterpart was left behind.
suggested_fix: Restate as measured, matching main.tex:392: "The leak fractions rose by up to 2.8x on the tasks large enough to have been capped (prom_core_all 0.0054 -> 0.0149); the median task moved 1.1x and the six registered tasks below the cap are unchanged."

claim: The same blockquote states the first GUE census capped training sets at 20,000 rows, "discarding 35-58% of train on seven tasks".
defect: Both the task count and the range are wrong, and both understate the truncation the passage is self-reporting. Nine registered tasks were truncated, not seven, and the discard fraction runs from 26.7% to 72.7%, so three truncated tasks fall below the stated 35% floor and one sits well above the stated 58% ceiling.
suggested_fix: Correct to "discarding 27-73% of train on nine of the fifteen registered tasks", or drop the range and state only the count and the maximum.

claim: The cross-suite NT census provenance line still says the train sets were capped at 20,000 and that every figure below is a lower bound.
defect: This is the exact defect that was the Round-15 blocker in the paper's Methods, fixed there but not in this artifact. The census was re-run uncapped; the committed CSV records no subsampling anywhere. The line therefore mislabels full-scale measurements as lower bounds, and directly contradicts paper/main.tex:322 ("We report this at full scale: an earlier pass capped training sets at 20,000..."). It is also self-contradictory in place: the table immediately beneath it (line 380) reports 6 borderline NT-original tasks, a tally that only exists at full scale — the capped pass returned 3 borderline and 5 clean (exp_crosssuite.log).
suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with the full-scale protocol, e.g. "Train sets uncapped (--cap 100000, above every task in both releases); no row is subsampled and no verdict is a lower bound. An earlier pass capped train at 20,000 and returned 3 borderline / 5 clean."

claim: The GUE full-scale re-run section states that uncapping made the leak fractions "rise roughly threefold".
defect: This is the same overstatement that was corrected in the paper last round (paper/main.tex:392 now reads "rose by up to $2.8\times$ ... the seven below the cap are of course unchanged"), left uncorrected in the findings artifact. "Roughly threefold" describes only the single largest ratio; it is not what the population of tasks did. A reader of this record takes away a systematically larger scale effect than the CSV supports, and the two committed artifacts now disagree about the size of the correction.
suggested_fix: Restate as measured, matching main.tex:392: "rose by up to 2.8x (prom_core_all 0.0054 -> 0.0149); the median task moved 1.2x and the six never-capped tasks are unchanged."

claim: The cross-suite summary table gives NT-revised a max jac@0.7 of 0.0020.
defect: Stale value carried over from the capped pass. The full-scale census puts the NT-revised maximum at 0.0030, so this row mixes a capped figure into a table whose NT-original row (max jac@0.7 0.2500, 6 borderline) is full-scale. The verdict is unaffected — both are far below the 0.1 cut — but the table's own numbers no longer trace to the CSV it names one line above.

claim: The same table reports NT-original as 13 tasks with 4 LEAKY, 6 borderline and 2 clean.
defect: The row does not sum: 4 + 6 + 2 = 12, against the 13 tasks the same row declares. The LEAKY and borderline columns are on the all-tasks basis while the clean column silently switches to the independent-task basis; the LEAKY column marks the switch as "4 (3)" but the clean column does not mark it at all. A reader reconciling the row against the CSV finds a missing task.
suggested_fix: Write the clean column as "3 (2)" so both bases are stated and both sum correctly (4+6+3=13, 3+6+2=11).

claim: The GUE re-run passage states the 20,000 cap discarded "35-58% of train on seven tasks".
defect: Both the count and the range understate the capping. Nine of the fifteen registered GUE tasks exceeded the cap, and the discarded fraction spans 26.7% to 72.7%. The stated 35-58% window silently excludes the two tasks with the smallest truncation and, more importantly, virus_covid, the most heavily truncated task at 72.7% — which is also the one task whose exact-duplicate fraction moved materially under the re-run (0.0394 -> 0.1219).
suggested_fix: Change to "discarding 27-73% of train on nine of the fifteen registered tasks".

claim: The released report card gives human_nontata_promoters an acc_drop_corrected of 0.108, and the generating module's comment asserts this value matches manuscript Table 2.
defect: Table 2 reports +0.118 for that dataset (the five-re-split-seed mean), while the released CSV carries 0.108 (the seed-0 bootstrap point estimate). The two differ by a full accuracy point on a headline number, and the code comment claiming they match is false. The paper does distinguish the two estimands at main.tex:212, but Table 2's own caption defines "Acc. lost" only as "the best-model accuracy change under the near-duplicate-aware re-split", so a reader diffing the released artifact against the table has no pointer to the difference. human_enhancers_ensembl is unaffected in practice (0.164 vs 0.165, a rounding difference).
suggested_fix: Either add an estimand column to the CSV (or a `_seed0` suffix on the field name) and correct the report_card.py comment, or add one clause to the Table 2 caption naming the five-seed mean and pointing at the seed-0 value the report card ships.

claim: §4 of the released findings document introduces the cross-suite census with: "`crosssuite_census.csv`, `crosssuite_exact_verification.csv`. Train sets capped at 20,000; capping only removes near-duplicate partners, so every figure is a lower bound." (lines 376-377)
defect: This is the exact defect the paper flags as an error it corrected, still asserted as current in the companion results document the paper's Availability statement points readers to. The census is uncapped: every row of results/crosssuite_census.csv has n_train_used == n_train_full and subsampled=False (e.g. promoter_no_tata 47767/47767, H3K4me3 33119/33119). The sentence is also self-contradicted twice inside its own file: the tally table two lines below it (line 382, "NT-original | 13 (11) | 4 (3) | 6 | 2") is the uncapped tally, and §4.2 at line 600 states "(An earlier capped pass reported 3 borderline and 5 clean; re-running uncapped moved three histone tasks across the containment cut.)" A referee opening the release sees the headline findings document assert a cap that main.tex §3.12 explicitly disclaims ("The census is run at full scale: no training set is subsampled"), and would reasonably conclude the paper's full-scale claim is unsupported by its own artifacts.
suggested_fix: Replace lines 376-377 with a full-scale statement ("Censused at full scale: n_train_used equals n_train available on every task; fractions remain lower bounds only for the length-cap reason of §3.4"), and add a check to audit/tools/check_numbers.py that fails if the string "capped at 20,000" appears in results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md §4 while crosssuite_census.csv has no subsampled row.

claim: The GUE full-scale re-run note states: "The first census capped training sets at 20,000 rows, discarding 35-58% of train on seven tasks... The leak fractions rose roughly threefold (`prom_core_all` 0.0054 -> 0.0149)" (lines 621-622).
defect: All three quantities are wrong in the same direction the paper corrected in round 15. Recomputing the capped census (git 3af3eb4:results/gue_census.csv) against the current one: nine registered tasks exceeded the cap, not seven (emp_H3K4me3, human_tf_0/1/3, prom_300_all/notata, prom_core_all/notata, virus_covid); the discarded share spans 26.7%-72.7%, not 35-58%; and the leak fractions did not rise "roughly threefold" - the maximum ratio is 2.77x, the median across changed task-metric pairs is about 1.55x, and seven of the seventeen censused tasks were never capped and are identical. The paper (main.tex:392) now correctly says "up to 2.8x on the tasks large enough to have been capped - the seven below the cap are of course unchanged", so the release contradicts the manuscript on the magnitude of its own self-correction.
suggested_fix: Rewrite lines 621-622 to match the manuscript: "discarding 27-73% of train on nine registered tasks... The leak fractions rose by up to 2.8x on the capped tasks (prom_core_notata 0.0079 -> 0.0219 under containment; median rise about 1.5x), and the seven tasks below the cap are unchanged."

claim: §3.3 registers P4 as "on a clean control no model's drop interval excludes zero" and §4.4 reports "P4 holds: on the clean control no model's drop interval excludes zero, for any of the nine" (main.tex:124, main.tex:246).
defect: The clean control is never named and its scale is never stated. It is human_enhancers_cohn run at n=20,000 - a 28% subsample of that dataset's 27,791 rows - while the two leaky arms of the same experiment are run at full scale (154,842 and 36,131) and Table 3 is captioned "full scale". This sits directly against the paper's own first practice recommendation ("Audit at full dataset scale, since subsampling can make a heavily leaky dataset look clean", main.tex:411) and against the Discussion's insistence that a capped run is not a measurement. The verdict is not in doubt - cohn's full-scale leak fraction is 0.0012 - but a referee scoring a pre-registered null on an undisclosed subsample of an unnamed dataset has a fair objection.
suggested_fix: In §4.4, name the control and its scale: "P4 holds: on the clean control (human_enhancers_cohn, n=20,000 of 27,791; full-scale leak fraction 0.001) no model's drop interval excludes zero, for any of the nine." Better, re-run the roster's clean arm at full scale so the paper's own scale rule is not broken by its own pre-registered control.

claim: §4.2 reports "the largest, drosophila_enhancers_stark RF, is +0.024 with 95% CI [-0.008,0.058]" (main.tex:212).
defect: Still open from round 15 (results/audit_findings.csv row 418, confirmed, unfixed). The point estimate is right but the interval matches no frozen recomputed artifact: both results/cluster_bootstrap_full.csv and results/bh_correction_frozen.csv give the stark RF cluster-bootstrap interval as [-0.0067, 0.0539], which rounds to [-0.007, 0.054]. The stated bounds appear only in the narrative results/NEW_FINDINGS.md:36, not in any computed CSV. The error is conservative and the verdict (interval covers zero, positive control holds) is unaffected, but this is the only clean-dataset interval quoted numerically in the paper and it cannot be regenerated from the release.
suggested_fix: Change $[-0.008,0.058]$ to $[-0.007,0.054]$ and pin it in audit/tools/check_numbers.py to the cluster_bootstrap_full.csv row so it cannot drift again.

claim: Referee verdict: MINOR REVISION. Biggest remaining weakness (not a defect to fix, a scope judgement the paper already discloses piecewise).
defect: The reordering claim - the paper's sole novel contribution, per §1 - rests on one dataset whose leakage is 38% literal byte-identical duplication (11,774 of 30,970 test rows), i.e. a gross curation bug rather than the subtle near-duplicate homology the title and abstract evoke. The second leaky dataset is conceded as cautionary-only; the one out-of-sample suite where the full pipeline ran produced no material inversion on any of three leaky tasks; and the paper's own condition attributes that null to delta<=0 on 22 of 24 pairs, which is a property of the comparison set rather than of the leakage. The construct-and-break manipulation is causally clean but reproduces the same extreme-duplication regime by construction. Each piece is disclosed honestly and in the same passage as the claim - which is why this is a nit and not a finding - but a reader who stops at the abstract will take "near-duplicate leakage can reorder model rankings on a genomic benchmark suite" as broader than n=1 in the byte-identical-duplication regime. The single most valuable follow-up remains the one the paper itself names: a replicated, interval-bearing CNN comparison, since the suite's own published baseline is a CNN and whether a CNN leaderboard is affected is currently open.
suggested_fix: No change required for acceptance. If the editor wants the title narrowed, "can reorder model rankings" -> "can reorder model rankings when a memorization-prone learner is compared" would align the title with the scope §4.3 and §5 already enforce.

claim: Introduction, scope paragraph for Claim II: "Both datasets on which we demonstrate it are short, fixed-length human regulatory sets, so we cannot rule that regime out as a further necessary condition---but it is certainly not a sufficient one, and \S\ref{sec:r-census} reports eleven tasks in exactly that regime---seven of them independent---pre-registered by us as leaky, that are clean."
defect: human_enhancers_ensembl is not fixed-length, and the paper says so twice elsewhere. Table 1 (main.tex:104) lists it as "269 (2--573)" under a caption that reads "Lengths are the median (with min--max range where variable)", and Methods 3.1 (main.tex:91) states "lengths are fixed within some datasets (e.g. 251 bp for human_nontata_promoters) and variable in others". The variability is not incidental to that dataset — it is load-bearing: the Table 1 caption and Methods 3.4 both build on its 2 bp minimum capping the length-pair Jaccard at ~0.004, which is the entire reason the containment re-measure exists and why 0.384 becomes 0.845. So the sentence that scopes the paper's central contribution asserts a shared property of the two demonstration datasets that the marquee one demonstrably lacks. This also inflates the parallel drawn in the same sentence: the eleven GUE tasks are genuinely fixed-length (70/101/300 bp), so they are not "in exactly that regime" as the regime is described here. The Discussion states the same argument correctly, using only "short-sequence regulatory benchmarks" (main.tex:403), which is the descriptor the evidence supports; the error is confined to this sentence and appears to be a residue of the earlier phrasing "short, fixed- or near-fixed-length" that audit_findings.csv rows 238/246/255/268 quote from a prior revision — the hedging qualifier was dropped when the sentence was rewritten, turning a defensible description into a false one.
suggested_fix: Restore the qualifier or drop the length descriptor: "Both datasets on which we demonstrate it are short human regulatory sets (one fixed-length at 251 bp, the other variable at 269 bp median, 2--573)". Then, since the eleven GUE tasks are fixed-length while one demonstration dataset is not, weaken "in exactly that regime" to the property the tasks actually share — short human regulatory sequence — matching the wording already used at main.tex:403.

claim: "The intraclass correlation is high ($0.91$--$0.99$) yet the design effect is small ($1.06$--$1.17$)".
defect: The design-effect range is taken over all four rows carrying an ICC/deff, but the ICC range is not: it silently drops the lowest of the four. Stating the two ranges in parallel in one clause tells the reader they summarise the same set of quantities, and one of them does not. The lowest ICC is 0.7794, not 0.91. The claim the sentence is making ("high ICC, small design effect") survives — 0.78 is still high — so this is a range-reporting error rather than a broken argument, but it is a number a referee can check in one line against the cited artifact.
suggested_fix: Change to "($0.78$--$0.99$)", or scope the clause to the random-forest rows if that is what was intended and give the deff range for the same two rows.

claim: Discussion, "What the detector detects, and one false positive": "four of the five clean Genomic Benchmarks datasets have a documented merge-and-deduplicate step and the fifth, \textit{demo\_human\_or\_worm}, is a cross-species disjoint draw; none has rows on duplicated coordinates."
defect: The universal "none" is false for the one dataset the sentence singles out. demo_human_or_worm's worm class carries a maximum coordinate multiplicity of 2 with 0.04% of its rows on a duplicated coordinate, and 0.03% of its test rows share an exact coordinate with train. The magnitude is negligible and does not weaken the argument — this passage uses coordinate-space cleanliness as k-mer-independent evidence for the estimator's floor, and 0.04% is three orders of magnitude below the leaky datasets' 94.3% — but the claim as written is an absolute and the artifact contradicts it, in the same passage that argues the coordinate evidence is the trustworthy independent channel.
suggested_fix: Soften to "none carries a material share of rows on duplicated coordinates (the largest, \textit{demo\_human\_or\_worm}, is $0.04\%$)".

claim: "We flag one scope limit squarely: this run is reported for `human_nontata_promoters` only, because the corresponding ensembl run exceeded our compute budget. It therefore establishes that leaky cross-validation selects the memorizing configuration on *a* leaky dataset, not yet on the specific dataset carrying the reordering claim."
defect: The ensembl tuning run completed and is committed. results/tuning_selection.csv rows 1-2 are human_enhancers_ensembl (naive_CV selects min_samples_leaf=1, grouped_CV selects 20), and exp_tuning_ens.log is dated 2026-07-19 02:03. paper/main.tex:382 devotes a full paragraph to that result and calls ensembl "the dataset carrying the reordering claim", reporting the 16.4-point vs 2.2-point contrast as the section's strongest evidence. The response-to-reviewers therefore concedes to Reviewer 3 that the decisive experiment was NOT run on the decisive dataset, when the manuscript in the same submission packet reports exactly that experiment. This is the same sentence HANDOFF.md:32 records as a round-8 blocker: it was corrected in main.tex and left standing here. check_numbers.py:377 registers "exceeded our compute budget" as a retired phrase, but DOCS (lines 43-47) does not include this file, so the gate reports PASS. cover_letter.md:22 carries the identical claim ("a tuning experiment we could afford on only one of the two leaky datasets — and it is `human_nontata_promoters`").
suggested_fix: Replace the scope-limit paragraph in R3.2 with the manuscript's §4.9 result (both datasets run; ensembl naive selects leaf=1 losing 16.4 points, grouped selects leaf=20 losing 2.2), and delete the corresponding clause in cover_letter.md:22. Rebuild both PDFs/DOCX via paper/build_letters.sh — the current artifacts are dated Jul 19 01:29, before the ensembl run finished.

claim: "Applying the census unchanged to the Nucleotide Transformer downstream tasks finds three of twelve independent tasks leaky, one at 25% byte-identical overlap." The same count appears at paper/response_to_reviewers.md:44 ("Three of twelve independent tasks are leaky").
defect: The independent-task denominator is eleven, not twelve. results/crosssuite_census.csv ships 13 NT-original tasks; two are nested (enhancers_types shares sequences with enhancers, and promoter_all is the exact union of promoter_no_tata and promoter_tata), leaving 11 independent: 3 LEAKY, 6 borderline, 2 clean. paper/main.tex states "three of eleven" at four sites (49, 71, 322, 409) and check_numbers.py:341-350 asserts it three times plus asserts "three of twelve" is absent. Both submission letters still carry the pre-collapse count, so the editor and reviewers read a denominator that contradicts the abstract of the manuscript in the same packet. "three of twelve" is registered as a retired phrase at check_numbers.py:369, but neither letter is in DOCS, and the match at response_to_reviewers.md:44 is capitalised ("Three of twelve"), which the case-sensitive matcher at check_numbers.py:382 would miss even if the file were registered.
suggested_fix: Change both letters to "three of eleven independent tasks leaky and six more borderline", matching main.tex:49. Then add cover_letter.md and response_to_reviewers.md to check_numbers.DOCS and lowercase both sides of the comparison in check_retired_claims (line 382).

claim: "**Both select min_samples_leaf = 1**, the memorizing default, with cross-validated accuracy falling monotonically as leaf size grows (0.914 → 0.786 naive, 0.823 → 0.783 grouped). Our own pre-registered expectation P5 — that the grouped procedure would select a more regularized forest — was **wrong**." Repeated at line 358 ("P5 fails outright") and cover_letter.md:20,22.
defect: P5 is scored differently in the two submitted documents. results/tuning_selection.csv shows grouped_CV selects min_samples_leaf=20 on human_enhancers_ensembl, so "both select 1" is true only of human_nontata_promoters — the quoted CV curves (0.9136→0.7856, 0.823→0.7834) are the nontata rows. paper/main.tex:124 and :384 accordingly score P5 as holding on human_enhancers_ensembl and tying on human_nontata_promoters. A reviewer who checks whether the authors honoured their pre-registration finds one document reporting a failure and the other a partial success on the same prediction. The prediction inventory is also inconsistent: response_to_reviewers.md:27 says "Four predictions (P1–P4) were committed", line 357 says "Of the five", and main.tex:124 scores six (P1–P6, P6 committed in the dose-response module). Separately, main.tex:124 explicitly declines to count P1's corrected-gap result as a confirmation ("we do not count this as a confirmation"), while response_to_reviewers.md:357 reports "P1 holds under the corrected gap".
suggested_fix: Rewrite the R3.2 second paragraph and the line-357 summary to the manuscript's scoring: six predictions committed, P5 holds on ensembl and ties on nontata, P1 fails as registered with the corrected-gap result labelled post hoc. Fix the "Four predictions (P1–P4)" inventory at line 27 and the parallel sentences in cover_letter.md:20,22.

claim: check_retired_claims docstring: "Statements the project has corrected, asserted absent from EVERY document. ... This is the systemic answer to the failure that produced the blocker in rounds 14, 15 and 16 ... Add to this list whenever a claim is retired, not just where it was found."
defect: The guard asserts absence across DOCS only, which registers three files (paper/main.tex, results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md, REPRODUCE.md — lines 43-47). paper/cover_letter.md and paper/response_to_reviewers.md are submitted to the journal alongside the manuscript and are not registered, so the three findings above sat under a green gate: `python -m audit.tools.check_numbers` reports 67/67 PASS while two retired phrases it explicitly lists ("three of twelve" line 369, "exceeded our compute budget" line 377) are live in the submission packet. This reproduces the round-13 defect class the module's own header names — "a docstring claiming coverage it did not have" (lines 9-13). Two secondary gaps compound it: the membership test at line 382 is case-sensitive, so response_to_reviewers.md:44's "Three of twelve" evades the check even after registration; and self_test() mutates only files in DOCS, so no mutation can demonstrate the letters are covered.
suggested_fix: Add "cover_letter": paper/cover_letter.md and "response": paper/response_to_reviewers.md to DOCS; lowercase both operands in check_retired_claims; add a self-test mutation targeting one of the newly registered letters so the coverage is proved non-vacuous. Consider also registering README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and HANDOFF.md with a per-phrase exemption for HANDOFF's historical narration, and amend the docstring to say "every registered document" with the registration list named.

claim: The response letter's answer to R3.2 states that both naive and cluster-grouped cross-validation select min_samples_leaf=1, that pre-registered prediction P5 was "wrong", and that the tuning run is reported for human_nontata_promoters only "because the corresponding ensembl run exceeded our compute budget".
defect: Every one of those three statements is the opposite of what the manuscript and the committed CSV say, on the dataset that carries the paper's central claim. results/tuning_selection.csv row 2: human_enhancers_ensembl / grouped_CV / selected_min_samples_leaf = 20 / acc_as_shipped 0.7513 / acc_corrected 0.7291. paper/main.tex:382 states this as a headline result ("Cluster-grouped cross-validation instead selects min_samples_leaf=20, and that model loses only 2.2 points (0.751->0.729)"), and paper/main.tex:124 and :384 score P5 as holding on human_enhancers_ensembl and tying on human_nontata_promoters. The ensembl run completed and is the decisive answer to R3.2 in the manuscript. The letter's cv_scores ("0.914 -> 0.786 naive, 0.823 -> 0.783 grouped") are the human_nontata_promoters row only, so the whole passage is written against a data state that no longer exists. The phrase "exceeded our compute budget" is on check_numbers.py's own retired list (HANDOFF.md:32 records it as a round-8 blocker fixed in main.tex) but the guard never scans this file. Consequence: a reviewer reading the response letter concludes the tuning objection was NOT answered on the dataset carrying the reordering claim, and sees the letter and manuscript assert contradictory results for the same experiment.
suggested_fix: Rewrite R3.2's second half and the cover letter's penultimate paragraph from results/tuning_selection.csv and paper/main.tex:382-384: grouped CV selects leaf=20 on ensembl (2.2-point drop vs the naive selection's 16.4) and ties at leaf=1 on nontata; P5 holds on ensembl and ties on nontata; there is no unfinished run. Update the P-count from five to six. Then add paper/cover_letter.md and paper/response_to_reviewers.md to check_numbers.py's DOCS map so the retired-claims group covers them, and rebuild via paper/build_letters.sh.

claim: Both submission letters report the Nucleotide Transformer census as "three of twelve independent tasks" leaky.
defect: The independent-task count was corrected to eleven in the manuscript (promoter_all is the exact union of promoter_no_tata and promoter_tata, so it is nested just as enhancers_types is; 13 shipped - 2 nested = 11). paper/main.tex:322 and :409 read "three of eleven", and check_numbers.py registers 'three of twelve' as a retired phrase — but its DOCS map (check_numbers.py:43-47) covers only main.tex, TIER1_FINDINGS.md and REPRODUCE.md, so the letters were never scanned. results/crosssuite_census.csv confirms 3 LEAKY / 6 borderline / 2 clean over the 11 independent tasks. This is the same half-applied-fix pattern that produced the largest finding in rounds 14, 15 and 16, now surviving in the documents an editor reads alongside the manuscript, and it under-reports the census denominator by one task in a passage the letter uses to argue the suite-level generality of the defect.
suggested_fix: Change both occurrences to "three of eleven", and state the six-borderline / two-clean split so the letters match paper/main.tex:322. Register the letters in check_numbers.py DOCS.

claim: The Discussion's scale caution says of the GUE census that "the seven below the cap are of course unchanged".
defect: results/gue_census.csv has 15 registered tasks, of which six have n_train_full <= 20000 (emp_H3 11971, emp_H4 11679, human_tf_2 19000, human_tf_4 19000, prom_300_tata 4904, prom_core_tata 4904). Seven is reachable only by including mouse_0 (6478), which is registered=False and which the paper elsewhere is careful to exclude from scoring. results/TIER1_FINDINGS.md:625 states the same quantity as "the six registered tasks below the cap", so the two live documents disagree on one number.
